events.title: Niall keeps his grandfather's stick at his own elbow
events.body: Niall takes down the hazel stick Calum kept since the night of An Diosal and sets it at his own writing-place rather than returning it to the shelf, though he puts it to no further use.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The sunwise turn

told_in.book: Of the Empty Harbour
told_in.section: I. Of the Boards Given Over

events.title: The rite of the empty harbour
events.body: A rite grows up about the quay the ships sailed from. It is still kept, lessened, on a day that none can now date truly.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The lamps kept on the rite's eve

events.title: The lamps kept on the rite's eve
events.body: On the eve nearest the day of An Diosal the households of Seann Skell bring small lights down to the west quay and set them along the stones the fleet sailed from, a rite grown up with no ordered beginning that Niall is the first to enter in the harbour-house's own leaves.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The rite of the empty harbour

told_in.book: Of the Empty Harbour
told_in.section: II. Of the Lamps Grown about the Berth

events.title: The harbour at half trade
events.body: The harbour-master of Seann Skell finds his berths at half their old use, for the fishing households that crewed the fleet are gone. The rope-walks of Cuan shean turn off hands for the first time.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Murchadh mac Raghnaill takes the berths

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The harbour-master's count of half trade

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The rope-walks of Cuan shean let hands go

events.title: The harbour-master's count of half trade
events.body: Murchadh mac Raghnaill, harbour-master of Seann Skell, sets his own reckoning of empty berths against full ones beside the boards: the harbour carries little more than half the trade it carried before An Diosal.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The harbour at half trade

told_in.book: Of the Empty Harbour
told_in.section: III. Of the Harbour at Half Trade

events.title: The rope-walks of Cuan shean let hands go
events.body: With more cordage made than the lessened harbour trade can use, the rope-walks along Cuan shean's waterfront turn off hands for the first time in the memory of any walker still living there.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The harbour at half trade

told_in.book: Of the Empty Harbour
told_in.section: III. Of the Harbour at Half Trade

events.title: The second silence
events.body: There is a rumour of a second, smaller crossing, with fewer ships and no word of where they went. Nothing that survives confirms or denies it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Word of a second, smaller crossing

events.title: Word of a second, smaller crossing
events.body: A hand off a coasting boat tells, at second or third remove, of a smaller fleet said to have sailed from the island's own shore in the years after An Diosal and never been heard from since. Niall hears the tale and, having no name or second mouth to stand behind it, sets it aside unwritten.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The second silence

told_in.book: Of the Empty Harbour
told_in.section: IV. Of the Word that Came and Was Not Written

events.title: The first turn of Faire a' Chinn
events.body: Seonag nic Dhùghaill of Ceann mhòr climbs the headland at first light and keeps it through the day, seeing nothing but open water. Other households take up a turn of their own after her, and the custom becomes Faire a' Chinn.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The watch at Ceann mhòr

told_in.book: Of the Empty Harbour
told_in.section: V. Of the Watch at Ceann mhòr

events.title: The west quay's old name falls from use
events.body: The plain old name of the west quay falls out of common mouths at Seann Skell as carters, fish-wives and children too young to have known the fleet come to call it Cidhe an Diosail, without any single day anyone can name for the change.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The west quay renamed

told_in.book: Of the Empty Harbour
told_in.section: VI. Of the New Name and the Old

events.title: The watch at Ceann mhòr
events.body: The fishing families of Ceann mhòr on the north-west coast keep a watch from the headland for returning sails, household by household in turn. The watch lapses within a generation. No sail is seen.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The first turn of Faire a' Chinn

events.title: The west quay renamed
events.body: The quay the ships sailed from is given a new name, so that common trade might go on under the old one without the memory. It is an early and quiet forgetting, made on purpose.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The west quay's old name falls from use

events.title: Cidhe an Diosail
events.body: The departure berth is entered in the harbour rolls of Seann Skell as Cidhe an Diosail, the quay of the sunwise turn. The name Cidhe an Iar passes to the new fish-wharf at the north end of the strand, and within a few years the fishers use it without a thought.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cidhe an Diosail entered in Rolla a' Chalaidh

events.title: Roghnaich takes its narrow sense
events.body: In the custody-book the verb roghnaich, to choose, begins to stand with no object, meaning to have chosen the crossing. The scribes of the next century use it so without explaining it, the surest sign that it had passed into common speech.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Roghnaich stands with no object

events.title: The first generation that never saw the fleet
events.body: Children born soon after the Setting-Out grow up never having seen the harbour with those ships in it. To them the leaving is already history.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Niall's own children who never saw the fleet

events.title: Cidhe an Diosail entered in Rolla a' Chalaidh
events.body: Niall enters the west quay's new name into Rolla a' Chalaidh in his own hand, letting the old name stand once beside it, struck through but not scraped. The old name, Cidhe an Iar, passes to the new fish-wharf at the strand's north end.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cidhe an Diosail

told_in.book: Of the Empty Harbour
told_in.section: VI. Of the New Name and the Old

events.title: Roghnaich stands with no object
events.body: In Rolla a' Chalaidh the word roghnaich, to choose, begins to stand alone in a clerk's hand, meaning to have chosen the crossing, and Niall lets the usage stand in his own leaves rather than write it out in full.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Roghnaich takes its narrow sense

told_in.book: Of the Empty Harbour
told_in.section: VI. Of the New Name and the Old

events.title: Niall's own children who never saw the fleet
events.body: Niall's eldest daughter, old enough by then to help about the harbour-house, asks whether he himself saw the ships go, having no memory of her own to set beside the wall of names she leans against.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first generation that never saw the fleet

told_in.book: Of the Empty Harbour
told_in.section: III. Of the Harbour at Half Trade

events.title: Death of Alasdair Saor and his last coaster
events.body: Alasdair mac Iain, Alasdair Saor, who laid the fleet's first deep keel, dies at Seann Skell at the end of summer, days after launching a sewn-plank coaster at Inis àrsaidh for a fish merchant there, his last work. Niall enters the death and the quay's new name on the same leaf.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Death of Alasdair Saor

told_in.book: Of the Empty Harbour
told_in.section: VIII. Of the Last Coaster and the Last Entry

events.title: Death of Alasdair Saor
events.body: Alasdair Saor, who laid the first deep keel, dies at Seann Skell. His last work was a coasting trader of the old sewn-plank kind, built for a fish merchant of Inis àrsaidh.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Death of Alasdair Saor and his last coaster

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Coinneach mac Fhearghais named master of the fellowship

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Death of Coinneach mac Fhearghais

events.title: Coinneach mac Fhearghais named master of the fellowship
events.body: After Alasdair Saor's death Coinneach mac Fhearghais, the first apprentice Alasdair ever swore, takes the mastership of the fellowship of the strand, keeping its oath and its coal exactly as Alasdair had kept them before him.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Alasdair Saor

told_in.book: Of the Moulds in the Fire
told_in.section: I. Of the Fellowship After Alasdair

events.title: Death of Coinneach mac Fhearghais
events.body: Coinneach mac Fhearghais dies at Seann Skell in the house where he had lived since his marriage, leaving the fellowship's coal to his eldest journeyman Griogair rather than to any man claiming it by right of years alone.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Alasdair Saor

told_in.book: Of the Moulds in the Fire
told_in.section: I. Of the Fellowship After Alasdair

events.title: The one household that breaks its own coal
events.body: By the seventieth year of the count Eachann Briseadair's is the only household on the hill below Taigh na Fèithe that does the whole of the breaking and sorting itself rather than hiring hands season by season.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The shipwrights' fellowship ends

told_in.book: Of the Moulds in the Fire
told_in.section: V. Of the Coal-Breakers Below the Hill

events.title: An Diosal count taken up at Cathair dhearg
events.body: The crown's own scribes at An Talla Dearg begin dating their rolls by the count Donnchadh mac Thormoid had kept alone at Taigh na Fèithe for near thirty years, setting aside the reckoning by a king's reign for the turning he first set his own hand to as a clerk of thirty.

told_in.book: Of the Moulds in the Fire
told_in.section: V. Of the Coal-Breakers Below the Hill

events.title: Eachann Briseadair raises the first house below Taigh na Fèithe
events.body: Eachann Briseadair, whose household breaks and sorts the coal brought down from the galleries, builds the first house of stone below Taigh na Fèithe's own gate; his sons build three more beside it within the decade, the beginning of the coal-breakers' row.

told_in.book: Of the Moulds in the Fire
told_in.section: V. Of the Coal-Breakers Below the Hill

events.title: Muileann dhearg a town in more than name
events.body: The coal-breakers' settlement below Taigh na Fèithe's gate, which has borne the name Muileann dhearg since the first years of the age, grows within Eachann Briseadair's lifetime into a town with its own well, smith and reeve, answering to Taigh na Fèithe rather than to any shire.

told_in.book: Of the Moulds in the Fire
told_in.section: V. Of the Coal-Breakers Below the Hill

events.title: The shipwrights' fellowship ends
events.body: No more sea-going ships being wanted, the fellowship that built the fleet of the Sundering quietly breaks up. Its craft is half forgotten by the time anyone needs it again.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The one household that breaks its own coal

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The fellowship of the strand released

events.title: The fellowship of the strand released
events.body: Griogair calls the fellowship's remaining journeymen to the strand and releases every man from the oath, judging there is no longer craft enough in the island's own boat-building to keep it; the journeymen scatter to the rope-walks, their fathers' land and Doire fhionn's coppice-cutting.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The shipwrights' fellowship ends

told_in.book: Of the Moulds in the Fire
told_in.section: II. Of the Last Journeymen and the Moulds Burned

events.title: The keel-moulds burned
events.body: In a hard season the patterns and moulds of the broken fellowship, kept in a shed on the strand at Seann Skell, are burned for firewood. The harbour-master notes the loss of the shed and not of what was in it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The keel-moulds burned for firewood

events.title: The keel-moulds burned for firewood
events.body: In the hard winter of Faolach the fellowship's old patterns and keel-moulds, untouched for years in the shed on the strand, are carried out and burned; the harbour-master notes only that the shed came down, and nothing of what it held.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The keel-moulds burned

told_in.book: Of the Moulds in the Fire
told_in.section: II. Of the Last Journeymen and the Moulds Burned

events.title: The lots drawn among Na Seachd Taighean
events.body: The heads of Na Seachd Taighean that hold the right to the coal are called to Taigh na Fèithe and each draws a marked stone from a covered bag before the custodians and the household, the galleries falling as the stones fall so that no house may claim its ground was given rather than drawn.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The mountain divided among the houses

told_in.book: Of the Moulds in the Fire
told_in.section: VI. Of the Lots Drawn Among the Seven Houses

events.title: Death of Raghnall mac Uilleim and the crowning of his son
events.body: Raghnall mac Uilleim dies in his eighty-fifth year after seven-and-thirty years on An Talla Dearg; his son Raghnall mac Raghnaill, seven-and-forty years old, is crowned in his place without dispute, Leabhar a' Chùraim giving the closed reign one line and the new one another.

told_in.book: Of the Moulds in the Fire
told_in.section: III. Of a King's Death and a Line in the Custody-Book

events.title: Birth of Ìomhar mac Raghnaill
events.body: In the year his grandfather dies and his father is crowned, a son, Ìomhar, is born at Cathair dhearg to Raghnall mac Raghnaill, a king of seven-and-forty with a new crown and a new child in the same season.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Raghnall dies; Ìomhar crowned

told_in.book: Of the Moulds in the Fire
told_in.section: III. Of a King's Death and a Line in the Custody-Book

events.title: Death of Eachann Briseadair
events.body: Eachann Briseadair dies at sixty in the shed where he broke his first load of coal as a boy, his sons and grandsons already keeping the work; he is buried on the rise above the row with a lump of unbroken coal set over him rather than a mason's stone.

told_in.book: Of the Moulds in the Fire
told_in.section: V. Of the Coal-Breakers Below the Hill

events.title: Death of Niall mac Dhòmhnaill
events.body: Niall mac Dhòmhnaill dies at Seann Skell in the harbour-house itself, six-and-forty years after taking up the boards, his grandfather's notched hazel stick set in his hand at his own asking and buried with him, the count it held never once spoken aloud.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The sunwise turn

told_in.book: Of the Moulds in the Fire
told_in.section: IV. Of the Death of Niall mac Dhòmhnaill

events.title: The mountain divided among the houses
events.body: The seven houses draw lots at the vein-house for the galleries each will keep, and the vein-house confirms each its Small-Burning measure. The lot-stones were kept in a bag at Muileann dhearg and shown to visitors for centuries after.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The lots drawn among Na Seachd Taighean

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Clachan a' Chrannchuir shown to a visitor

events.title: The coppice law of Doire fhionn
events.body: The great oaks gone to the fleet, the shire of Doire fhionn forbids the felling of any living oak without the reeve's mark and begins to cut its woods by coppice. The law spreads to every shire with a Doire in its name.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The Child walled

events.title: The lamps kept at Seann Skell
events.body: The waterfront of Seann Skell keeps the night of lamps each year on the eve of the rite of the empty harbour. The children are told the lamps are for ships coming home, and the priests do not gainsay it.

events.title: Death of Donnchadh mac Thormoid
events.body: Donnchadh mac Thormoid, the vein-house scribe who began the count of years, dies at Muileann dhearg. His last entry is the season's burning of coal, household by household, in the same hand as his first.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Death of Donnchadh mac Thormoid

events.title: Clachan a' Chrannchuir shown to a visitor
events.body: Old Donnchadh takes the bag of Clachan a' Chrannchuir down from its peg to let a grandson of Eachann Briseadair's, waiting idle in Taigh na Fèithe hall, hold it and hear how the seven heads once drew their galleries, though he tells the boy nothing of which stone fell to which house.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The mountain divided among the houses

told_in.book: Of the Moulds in the Fire
told_in.section: VII. Of the Stones Shown to a Visitor

events.title: Death of Donnchadh mac Thormoid
events.body: Donnchadh mac Thormoid dies at Muileann dhearg in his ninety-fifth year, his last entry the season's burning of coal household by household, set down in the same careful hand he had used since he was fifteen.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Donnchadh mac Thormoid

told_in.book: Of the Moulds in the Fire
told_in.section: V. Of the Coal-Breakers Below the Hill

events.title: Raghnall dies; Ìomhar crowned
events.body: King Raghnall mac Raghnaill dies at Cathair dhearg, and his son Ìomhar mac Raghnaill is crowned. Raghnall had followed his father Raghnall mac Uilleim, who died in his eighty-fifth year after a long and quiet reign; the custody-book gives each of the two Raghnalls a single line.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of Raghnall mac Raghnaill

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of Ìomhar mac Raghnaill

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The old men compare two crownings

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: The king's habit at the gallery's mouth

events.title: The old men compare two crownings
events.body: At Cathair dhearg the court remarks that Ìomhar mac Raghnaill's crowning differs little from his father's three-and-thirty years before, the same cup passed hand to hand and the same oath said over it, a quiet continuity Leabhar a' Chùraim itself gives only a single line apiece.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Raghnall dies; Ìomhar crowned

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: I. Of Two Lines in One Book

events.title: A boy of Inis mhòr asks why the barges keep the coast
events.body: Watching the first grain barge loaded on the Abhainn ghorm, a boy of Inis mhòr asks his father why the boat should not simply cross open water by the shorter way, and is answered only with a look and no word, for no one on the island since the fleet has wished to be out of sight of land.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Inis mhòr's grain fleet

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: I. Of Two Lines in One Book

events.title: The silversmiths of Muileann chiar
events.body: Silver of the seam at Muileann chiar, mined since the Holy Age, is wrought into neck-rings for the heads of the seven houses. The smiths' fellowship of the seam, heirs of Sliochd Fhearchair, keeps its craft within four families.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first silver neck-rings worn

events.title: The first silver neck-rings worn
events.body: The heads of Na Seachd Taighean first wear the neck-rings beaten by the smiths of Muileann chiar, so that a stranger at Taigh na Fèithe or An Talla Dearg may know a custodian by the collar at his throat before a word is said.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The silversmiths of Muileann chiar

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: I. Of Two Lines in One Book

events.title: Inis mhòr's grain fleet
events.body: Inis mhòr in the north builds barges to carry grain down the Abhainn ghorm to Caol bheag, and from Ros chiar at the river mouth west along the coast to Cnoc bheag. They are sewn-plank boats of the old kind, and none lies a night out of sight of land.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A boy of Inis mhòr asks why the barges keep the coast

events.title: The coughing sickness at Caol fhiadhaich
events.body: A coughing sickness runs through Caol fhiadhaich on the south-west coast and kills some ten before it burns out. The shared meal is kept throughout, and the reeve holds that it saved the rest.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The shared meal kept through the cough

events.title: The shared meal kept through the cough
events.body: When the coughing sickness reaches the reeve's own household at Caol fhiadhaich, his wife refuses to let their door be barred against the shared board, holding that a household which eats apart out of fear will go on eating apart after the fear has passed; she lives, and the custom outlasts the sickness.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The coughing sickness at Caol fhiadhaich

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: I. Of Two Lines in One Book

events.title: Birth of Fearchar mac Lachlainn
events.body: A son, Fearchar, is born in the house of Clann Fhearchair at Baile Mòr dhomhain, the elder of two brothers, in a hall that has never looked for a crown and does not look for one now.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Fearchar mac Lachlainn chosen

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: III. Of the Silences in the Yard

events.title: The king's habit at the gallery's mouth
events.body: King Ìomhar takes up a habit no ruler before him is recorded keeping, asking the youngest hand at any gallery he visits to name the prop, the cut and the tally-mark before him; Taigh na Fèithe's scribe judges it a kind of counting of his own, made by a king with no child to leave the hall to.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: Raghnall dies; Ìomhar crowned

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: I. Of Two Lines in One Book

events.title: A singing timber clears the gallery
events.body: Bound as a child to a custodian's household, Fearchar mac Lachlainn stands outside a mountain gallery in the night while the custodian, hearing a timber begin to sing, has the working cleared an hour before the prop gives way with no one beneath it; he keeps the memory into his own old age.

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: II. Of a Boy at Baile Mòr dhomhain

events.title: Am Buabhall Fortanach rebuilt in stone
events.body: The old road-house of Am Buabhall Fortanach burns to its footings, and its keeper, Eilidh nic Chaluim, rebuilds it in stone. It is already known for its jugged buffalo.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Am Buabhall Fortanach's new stone walls

events.title: Am Buabhall Fortanach's new stone walls
events.body: Eilidh nic Chaluim raises the burned road-house of Am Buabhall Fortanach again in stone, and a boy of Clann Fhearchair riding out with his father to see the walls going up is given a bowl of the jugged buffalo before the roof itself is finished.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Am Buabhall Fortanach rebuilt in stone

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: II. Of a Boy at Baile Mòr dhomhain

events.title: Fearchar mac Lachlainn bound to the galleries
events.body: At seven years old Fearchar mac Lachlainn is bound for seven years to a custodian's household above Muileann dhearg, as every child of Na Seachd Taighean is meant to be, while his younger brother Iain is kept at home to learn the hall.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearchar mac Lachlainn chosen

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: II. Of a Boy at Baile Mòr dhomhain

events.title: Death of Raghnall Beag mac Ìomhair
events.body: King Ìomhar's only son, Raghnall Beag, dies of a fever at Cathair dhearg; a custodian of Clann Fhearchair reads the letter aloud and says that a king with no other child is a house with one wall standing, which the wind will find sooner or later.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ìomhar dies without an heir

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: II. Of a Boy at Baile Mòr dhomhain

events.title: Fearchar comes home from the galleries
events.body: Fearchar mac Lachlainn comes home to Baile Mòr dhomhain at fourteen, able to tell the weight of a sealed measure by its heft and the sound a gallery makes when its timbering has begun to fail.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearchar mac Lachlainn chosen

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: II. Of a Boy at Baile Mòr dhomhain

events.title: The spirit-house at Dùn ìseal
events.body: The keepers of the Old Spirits, the faith of the hearths, raise a house for the ancestors at Dùn ìseal, and cut the names of the dead of the eastern shires on wooden posts. The posts are cut anew each generation as the old ones rot.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Names cut new on the posts of Dùn ìseal

events.title: Names cut new on the posts of Dùn ìseal
events.body: A young man of Clann Fhearchair, travelling east with his father, stands long before the wooden posts of the spirit-house at Dùn ìseal, reading names the shire itself cuts anew each generation, and says only that a shire which trusts wood to hold its dead must trust its own memory further than he would.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The spirit-house at Dùn ìseal

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: II. Of a Boy at Baile Mòr dhomhain

events.title: The head of Clann Fhearchair names his younger son
events.body: The head of Clann Fhearchair dies at Baile Mòr dhomhain, naming his younger son Iain mac Lachlainn to the headship of the house and leaving his elder son Fearchar to the galleries he knows.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearchar mac Lachlainn chosen

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: II. Of a Boy at Baile Mòr dhomhain

events.title: Ìomhar dies without an heir
events.body: King Ìomhar mac Raghnaill dies at Cathair dhearg with no living child, and with him ends the line of Beathag. The heads of the seven houses are summoned to the capital to name a king.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Death of Raghnall Beag mac Ìomhair

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The heads of the seven summoned to the capital

events.title: The heads of the seven summoned to the capital
events.body: With King Ìomhar dead and no living child of his line, riders carry word to all of Na Seachd Taighean that their heads are summoned to Cathair dhearg to choose, for the first time since An Diosal, a king the crown's own blood cannot simply hand down.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ìomhar dies without an heir

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearchar mac Lachlainn chosen

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: II. Of a Boy at Baile Mòr dhomhain

events.title: Fearchar mac Lachlainn chosen
events.body: The heads of the houses choose Fearchar mac Lachlainn of Baile Mòr dhomhain, of Clann Fhearchair, and he is crowned at Cathair dhearg. He is the first king made by the seven houses and not by descent.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of Fearchar mac Lachlainn

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Fearchar mac Lachlainn bound to the galleries

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Fearchar comes home from the galleries

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The head of Clann Fhearchair names his younger son

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The heads of the seven summoned to the capital

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain mac Lachlainn turns the choosing aside

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A borrowed cup for the first oath

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The head of Clann Ìomhair breaks the silence in the yard

events.title: Iain mac Lachlainn turns the choosing aside
events.body: Named by the other heads as a possible king, Iain mac Lachlainn of Clann Fhearchair turns the honour aside, saying a man who keeps one house's hall well may yet keep a kingdom poorly, and names his elder brother Fearchar in his place.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Fearchar mac Lachlainn chosen

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: III. Of the Silences in the Yard

events.title: A borrowed cup for the first oath
events.body: With no cup of the crown's own ready for the rite, the head of Clann Mhuirich sends for the cup her own house keeps, so that Fearchar mac Lachlainn drinks his first oath as king from a vessel that belongs, strictly, to one house among the seven rather than to the crown.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Fearchar mac Lachlainn chosen

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: III. Of the Silences in the Yard

events.title: The head of Clann Ìomhair breaks the silence in the yard
events.body: After a morning's silence in the yard of An Talla Dearg the head of Clann Ìomhair speaks first: the line of Beathag has held the hall a hundred years and more, and no house of the seven has a better claim to it than another.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Fearchar mac Lachlainn chosen

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: III. Of the Silences in the Yard

events.title: Birth of Fearchar Donn
events.body: A son is born to King Fearchar mac Lachlainn, then one-and-thirty and six years crowned, and is called Fearchar Donn for the brown of his hair; he is the first child born to a king Na Seachd Taighean chose.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Fearchar Donn crowned

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: III. Of the Silences in the Yard

events.title: A court at Baile Mòr dhomhain
events.body: King Fearchar keeps his court part of each year at Baile Mòr dhomhain, near the mountain, that he may take counsel of the vein-house without a journey. The double court lasts as long as his house.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The double court divided

events.title: The double court divided
events.body: King Fearchar settles the custom of keeping his court partly at Cathair dhearg and partly at Baile Mòr dhomhain near Taigh na Fèithe, with his brother Iain keeping Clann Fhearchair's own hall whenever the court is away at the capital.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A court at Baile Mòr dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: IV. Of the Double Court

events.title: Fearchar Donn asked the child's question
events.body: Brought young to the mountain as his father had been, Fearchar Donn is asked at seven years old to name the prop, the cut and the tally-mark before him at a gallery's mouth, and gives an answer his father calls, laughing, the first honestly ordinary thing his own house has produced in two reigns.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearchar Donn crowned

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: IV. Of the Double Court

events.title: The brothers' leaf-book of letters
events.body: A later hand at Baile Mòr dhomhain gathers into one leaf-book the letters King Fearchar and his brother Iain exchange across every season of the divided court, boundary disputes and grain petitions set down beside a long-running complaint over the capital's cooking.

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: IV. Of the Double Court

events.title: The fishers of Àth fhiadhaich
events.body: After a season of losses the fishing families of Àth fhiadhaich join in one fellowship to share boats and nets. It is the first fishers' fellowship on the east coast.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A fisherman questioned on the fellowship

events.title: A fisherman questioned on the fellowship
events.body: Brought before the old king almost by chance, a fisherman of Àth fhiadhaich is kept a full hour answering questions on how boats and nets are shared among the new fellowship's households, and rides home understanding only afterward that the king was asking after the fellowship itself, not the fish.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fishers of Àth fhiadhaich

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: IV. Of the Double Court

events.title: Fearchar Donn crowned
events.body: Fearchar mac Lachlainn dies, and his son, called Fearchar Donn, is crowned at Cathair dhearg without dispute.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of Fearchar Donn

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Fearchar Donn asked the child's question

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A king's fire kept to the ordinary measure

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: Na Seachd Taighean stand at Clann Fhearchair's grave

events.title: A king's fire kept to the ordinary measure
events.body: Dying, King Fearchar asks that no coal be burned beyond the ordinary handful for any rite made over him, and Taigh na Fèithe keeps the asking to the letter, so that the fire lit for a king is no larger than the fire any house of the seven lights for its own dead.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Fearchar Donn crowned

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: IV. Of the Double Court

events.title: Na Seachd Taighean stand at Clann Fhearchair's grave
events.body: The heads of Na Seachd Taighean, each still wearing the neck-ring of Muileann chiar, stand at the grave of the king they chose nine-and-twenty years before, and not one of them is heard to say the choosing made in that cold yard was anything other than the right one.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: Fearchar Donn crowned

told_in.book: Of the King the Houses Made
told_in.section: IV. Of the Double Court

events.title: A hawk overfed will not come to the glove
events.body: A young bird of the mews at Cnoc bheag, fed too heavy the evening before, will not answer Gormshuil nic Artair's call at the dawn rite; her father Artair, too stiff now to climb to the block himself, tells her plainly that a bird fed past its measure is as useless as one starved of it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gormshuil of the Hawk

told_in.book: Of the Hawk of Acaill
told_in.section: I. Of the Glove at Cnoc bheag

events.title: Gormshuil calls Mòd down alone for the first time
events.body: With Artair's knees failed for the climb, Gormshuil nic Artair goes up to the mews block at Cnoc bheag before dawn and calls the shrine's hawk down with no one else to answer for the flight, three-and-thirty years old and, by her own later word, more frightened coming down than going up.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gormshuil of the Hawk

told_in.book: Of the Hawk of Acaill
told_in.section: I. Of the Glove at Cnoc bheag

events.title: Death of Artair, hawk-keeper of Cnoc bheag
events.body: Artair dies at Cnoc bheag in his own bed above the shrine, three-score and ten years old, and the keeping of the mews he had held the better part of his life passes without dispute to his daughter Gormshuil; the hill's households bury him facing the shrine rather than in any rite of the departed.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gormshuil of the Hawk

told_in.book: Of the Hawk of Acaill
told_in.section: II. Of the Empty Perch

events.title: Gormshuil first names the vein An Seabhag Acrach
events.body: Asked, as custom wants, to say a few words over her father's empty place on the bench, Gormshuil nic Artair tells the shrine's watchers for the first time that the vein under Muileann dhearg is itself a hawk of Mòd's kind, to be fed the measured handful and never glutted past it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gormshuil of the Hawk

told_in.book: Of the Hawk of Acaill
told_in.section: II. Of the Empty Perch

events.title: Hawk-keepers of the north coast come to hear her
events.body: Word of Gormshuil's teaching, carried inland by a wool-buyer of Bàgh an t-Seabhaig, brings three keepers of the coastal shrines to Cnoc bheag to judge it for themselves; they stay a week among the coal-cutters' wives at the shrine's ledge and go home saying the teaching has lost nothing in the carrying.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gormshuil of the Hawk

told_in.book: Of the Hawk of Acaill
told_in.section: III. Of Those Who Came to Hear

events.title: Bàgh an t-Seabhaig elder questions Gormshuil's own hunger
events.body: The eldest of the three coastal keepers asks Gormshuil, on the last morning of their visit, whether she has ever gone hungry enough herself to know the second half of what she teaches; Gormshuil answers that she has, twice, and disliked the lesson both times without forgetting either.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gormshuil of the Hawk

told_in.book: Of the Hawk of Acaill
told_in.section: III. Of Those Who Came to Hear

events.title: Gormshuil of the Hawk
events.body: At Cnoc bheag, where the dawn-hawk rite of the Holy Age is still kept, the priestess Gormshuil nic Artair teaches that the hawk of the rite is Mòd, the Hawk of Acaill, as old as Fionntan mac Bòchra, eldest of men, and remembering all things with him. The vein, she teaches, is the Hungry Hawk, to be fed the measured handful and no more, for a hawk overfed will not hunt and a hawk starved will turn on the hand. Her followers gather the old rite into the first house of Òrd an t-Seabhaig, the order of the Hawk of Acaill.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A hawk overfed will not come to the glove

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Gormshuil calls Mòd down alone for the first time

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Death of Artair, hawk-keeper of Cnoc bheag

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Gormshuil first names the vein An Seabhag Acrach

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Hawk-keepers of the north coast come to hear her

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Bàgh an t-Seabhaig elder questions Gormshuil's own hunger

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gormshuil's first true congregation

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Taigh an t-Seabhaig raised

events.title: Gormshuil's first true congregation
events.body: The watchers climbing to Cnoc bheag for the dawn rite grow past the number the shrine's ledge can easily hold, and Gormshuil, asked more mornings than not to give the teaching whole, gathers it at last into the shape it will keep for the rest of her life.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Gormshuil of the Hawk

told_in.book: Of the Hawk of Acaill
told_in.section: III. Of Those Who Came to Hear

events.title: Taigh an t-Seabhaig raised
events.body: Gormshuil's watchers, calling themselves a house rather than a congregation, raise a hall of timber and dry stone below the mews block at Cnoc bheag, giving the old dawn-hawk rite a roof of its own for the first time in its keeping.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Gormshuil of the Hawk

told_in.book: Of the Hawk of Acaill
told_in.section: III. Of Those Who Came to Hear

events.title: The hawk-house at Ros gheal
events.body: Gormshuil's pupils found a second house of the Hawk at Ros gheal. Its priests take charge of the measured burning for all the country between Ros gheal on the coast and Cnoc bheag up the river.

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: The hawk-faithful carry the customs officer out of Ros gheal

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A second house raised at Ros gheal

events.title: A second house raised at Ros gheal
events.body: Two of Gormshuil's pupils, a brother and sister of a coastal household, carry the dawn rite down to the shore at Ros gheal rather than make every fisher's family of that coast walk two days inland; Gormshuil goes down herself to judge the teaching had travelled whole.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hawk-house at Ros gheal

told_in.book: Of the Hawk of Acaill
told_in.section: IV. Of the House at Ros gheal and the Flood at Seann Vell

events.title: Birth of Sìleas nic Fhearchair
events.body: A daughter, Sìleas, is born at Cathair dhearg to King Fearchar Donn in the two-and-thirtieth year of his reign, when he is five-and-fifty years old; she is his only child to live.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Queen Sìleas's measures

told_in.book: Of the Hawk of Acaill
told_in.section: I. Of the Glove at Cnoc bheag

events.title: Flood at Seann Vell
events.body: In a wet spring the river at Seann Vell on the south-east coast breaks its banks and carries away the lower mills. The mill-wrights build them again on the higher bank.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A pupil reports the flood at Seann Vell

events.title: A pupil reports the flood at Seann Vell
events.body: A pupil of the Ros gheal house, present on other business when the river at Seann Vell breaks its banks and carries away the lower mills, calls the flood a kind of overfed hawk; Gormshuil tells him plainly that a river is a river and not a hawk, and sends him back to watch the mills rebuilt before he judges further.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Flood at Seann Vell

told_in.book: Of the Hawk of Acaill
told_in.section: IV. Of the House at Ros gheal and the Flood at Seann Vell

events.title: Death of Gormshuil nic Artair
events.body: Gormshuil dies at Cnoc bheag, two-and-sixty years old, in the season the house at Ros gheal marks its own eighth year, and is buried, at her own asking, on the open hillside beside her father rather than within the hall her own teaching raised.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The sayings of Gormshuil written

told_in.book: Of the Hawk of Acaill
told_in.section: V. Of the Marked Sayings

events.title: Ùisdean mac Pàdraig marks the sayings he did not hear
events.body: Gathering Gormshuil's teaching into a single book, Ùisdean mac Pàdraig travels as far as Ros gheal to set down what her pupils remember, marking plainly every saying he did not hear from her own mouth; when the book is finished the marked sayings far outnumber the rest.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The sayings of Gormshuil written

told_in.book: Of the Hawk of Acaill
told_in.section: V. Of the Marked Sayings

events.title: The sayings of Gormshuil written
events.body: After Gormshuil's death her sayings are written at Cnoc bheag as Leabhar an t-Seabhaig, the Book of the Hawk. The copyist, Ùisdean mac Pàdraig, marks every saying he did not hear from her own mouth, and these are the greater part.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Death of Gormshuil nic Artair

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Ùisdean mac Pàdraig marks the sayings he did not hear

events.title: The death of King Fearchar Donn
events.body: Fearchar Donn dies at Cathair dhearg in his sixty-eighth year, the last of his own riding to Taigh na Fèithe's winter burning long past. His daughter Sìleas, thirteen years old, is judged too young to be crowned, and the heads of the seven custodian houses take the hall in her name by turns.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Queen Sìleas's measures

told_in.book: Of the Firlot of Cathair dhearg
told_in.section: I. Of the Girl Who Counted the Baskets

events.title: Sìleas nic Fhearchair crowned
events.body: Sìleas, fifteen years old, is crowned at Cathair dhearg with the same cup and the same oath as her father before her. The heads of Na Seachd Taighean swear over her hands to hold the vein and its right as it has always been held.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Queen Sìleas's measures

told_in.book: Of the Firlot of Cathair dhearg
told_in.section: II. Of the Crowning at Fifteen

events.title: The storm that took Seann Toll's boats
events.body: A northern storm, named Am Fuath Mòr in the harbour rolls, breaks the harbour wall of Seann Toll and sinks forty boats at their moorings. Eighteen fishers drown.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall mac Nèill in the water at Seann Toll

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The dead of Am Fuath Mòr buried on the headland

events.title: Raghnall mac Nèill in the water at Seann Toll
events.body: In the storm the north coast calls Am Fuath Mòr, Raghnall mac Nèill, reeve of Seann Toll, thirty-four years old and four years in office, stands knee-deep on the strand hauling on a rope with three other men to bring in a boat with two children lashed inside it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The storm that took Seann Toll's boats

told_in.book: Of the Firlot of Cathair dhearg
told_in.section: III. Of Am Fuath Mòr and the Hooked Wall

events.title: The dead of Am Fuath Mòr buried on the headland
events.body: Seann Toll buries the eighteen who drowned trying to save the boats in a single row on the headland above the broken wall, a row so long that the reeve keeping the count loses his place twice and begins again.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The storm that took Seann Toll's boats

told_in.book: Of the Firlot of Cathair dhearg
told_in.section: III. Of Am Fuath Mòr and the Hooked Wall

events.title: The queen weds Dùghall mac Ìomhair
events.body: Sìleas takes a consort of her own choosing, Dùghall mac Ìomhair of the eastern hill-house Clann Ìomhair, whom she has known since the years of her regency. Na Seachd Taighean' heads attend the wedding at Cathair dhearg.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The walls of Dùn dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Firlot of Cathair dhearg
told_in.section: IV. Of the Walls of Dùn dhearg and a Supper Kept Cold

events.title: Seann Toll walls its harbour again
events.body: Seann Toll builds its harbour wall again, higher and with a hooked end, to a plan the reeve had from the masons of the capital. The wall stands through every storm of this age.

events.title: The walls of Dùn dhearg
events.body: Clann Ìomhair, who hold the land about Dùn dhearg in the eastern hills, wall it in stone. These are the first walls on the island raised by a custodian house and not by the crown.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The queen weds Dùghall mac Ìomhair

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A cold supper at An Talla Dearg

events.title: Queen Sìleas's measures
events.body: Sìleas nic Fhearchair, crowned after her father Fearchar Donn, fixes one measure for grain across the island, the firlot of Cathair dhearg, so that barter between shires need not begin with a quarrel over the size of a basket. Firlots of oak bound with iron are sent to every shire seat.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of Sìleas nic Fhearchair

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The death of King Fearchar Donn

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Sìleas nic Fhearchair crowned

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The quarrel over a basket at the capital's market

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The firlots carried to the shire seats

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first quarrel settled by the firlot

events.title: A cold supper at An Talla Dearg
events.body: Sìleas summons the head of Clann Ìomhair to a supper at Cathair dhearg after his house walls Dùn dhearg without the crown's leave. Neither speaks plainly of the walls; both understand what is meant by everything left unsaid, and the walls stand unopposed.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The walls of Dùn dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Firlot of Cathair dhearg
told_in.section: IV. Of the Walls of Dùn dhearg and a Supper Kept Cold

events.title: The quarrel over a basket at the capital's market
events.body: Watching a farmer and a grain-seller come near to blows below An Talla Dearg over the true size of a basket, Sìleas is put in mind of a like quarrel she watched as a child, and resolves that one measure alone shall serve the whole island.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Queen Sìleas's measures

told_in.book: Of the Firlot of Cathair dhearg
told_in.section: V. Of the Quarrel over a Basket

events.title: The firlots carried to the shire seats
events.body: Oak firlots bound with three iron hoops, each cut to the capital's standard and marked with the queen's own mark, go out by cart from Cathair dhearg to every shire seat on the island, so that a basket weighed true at the capital weighs true anywhere a Dia-thìrich stands to sell or buy.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Queen Sìleas's measures

told_in.book: Of the Firlot of Cathair dhearg
told_in.section: V. Of the Quarrel over a Basket

events.title: The first quarrel settled by the firlot
events.body: At Àth shean a carter and a miller who have fallen out over a load of oats are measured true against the town's firlot before a crowd their shouting drew, and the matter is settled before either of them thinks to shout further.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Queen Sìleas's measures

told_in.book: Of the Firlot of Cathair dhearg
told_in.section: V. Of the Quarrel over a Basket

events.title: Birth of Uisdean mac Dhùghaill
events.body: Sìleas and Dùghall's son Uisdean is born at Cathair dhearg, a quiet and watchful child who is one day to follow his mother in the hall.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Death of Queen Sìleas

told_in.book: Of the Firlot of Cathair dhearg
told_in.section: VI. Of the Tally-Houses and the Long City's Market

events.title: Tally-houses in the royal granaries
events.body: Queen Sìleas sets a tally-house in each royal granary, where every exchange of grain for cloth, salt or labour is cut on paired sticks, one for each party. It is the first reckoning of trade across the whole island, and it runs without coin.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A trader questions the tally-stick at Cathair dhearg

events.title: A trader questions the tally-stick at Cathair dhearg
events.body: At the granary tally-house a trader of the long city asks the clerk what stops a false notch being cut after a bargain is struck, and is shown how the grain of a split stick runs true only when its two halves are laid together again.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tally-houses in the royal granaries

told_in.book: Of the Firlot of Cathair dhearg
told_in.section: VI. Of the Tally-Houses and the Long City's Market

events.title: The market charter of Cathair fhada
events.body: Queen Sìleas grants Cathair fhada a market on its ridge at every full moon, with a tally-house for the south; it is the first market right cut on paired sticks. The merchants of the long city carry the honey, hemp, wax and pots of the south to the capital, and begin to go as one company to the harvest fair at Muileann òg.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first full-moon market at Cathair fhada

events.title: The first full-moon market at Cathair fhada
events.body: Under the new charter the long city holds its first market timed to the full moon, and traders come from three days' walk in every direction to carry honey, hemp, wax and pottery north as one company.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The market charter of Cathair fhada

told_in.book: Of the Firlot of Cathair dhearg
told_in.section: VI. Of the Tally-Houses and the Long City's Market

events.title: Drochaid Cathair dhearg widened
events.body: The old stone bridge over Abhainn dhomhain at Cathair dhearg is widened for two carts to pass. Queen Sìleas's name is cut on the downstream parapet, and may still be read there.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The bridge of Cathair dhearg widened

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Sìleas rides to the widened bridge with her son

events.title: The bridge of Cathair dhearg widened
events.body: The old stone bridge over Abhainn dhomhain at Cathair dhearg is widened for two loaded carts to pass abreast, and the queen's name is cut into the downstream parapet without her asking for it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Drochaid Cathair dhearg widened

told_in.book: Of the Firlot of Cathair dhearg
told_in.section: VII. Of the Bridge

events.title: Sìleas rides to the widened bridge with her son
events.body: On a grey morning in Bearnach Queen Sìleas rides down to see Drochaid Cathair dhearg finished, widened for two carts abreast, forty-six years old, with her son Uisdean, nineteen, riding at her side.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Drochaid Cathair dhearg widened

told_in.book: Of the Firlot of Cathair dhearg
told_in.section: VII. Of the Bridge

events.title: Coinneach mac Mhàrtainn on the carters' roads
events.body: Coinneach mac Mhàrtainn, a druid of the schools of Flidais who has walked the roads of the middle shires for the better part of forty years, carries the stag's teaching from house to house with a stick, a satchel of writing-boards and no fixed hearth.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: An Leòmhann Buidhe on the north road

told_in.book: Of Carson an Làmh Seo
told_in.section: I. Of the Carters' Roads

events.title: The crossing days of the panthers
events.body: In the southern hills near Imrich nam Pantar the herders keep the panther roads clear on the days the great cats cross, and drive their flocks off the paths beforehand. The crossing days are the first thing the southern shires agree on in writing.

links.label: Same place
links.title: Coinneach among the panther-herders

events.title: An Leòmhann Buidhe on the north road
events.body: An Leòmhann Buidhe, a road-house on the northern mining road, serves the coal-carters oatcakes fried in linseed oil, and fire water. Its keeper is fined for watering the fire water.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Coinneach mac Mhàrtainn on the carters' roads

links.label: Same place
links.title: Coinneach hears the carters' grumbling at An Leòmhann Buidhe

events.title: Coinneach among the panther-herders
events.body: Travelling south into the panther country in the season of the crossing, Coinneach mac Mhàrtainn finds a whole valley emptied of flocks and every gate on the panthers' path standing open. An old herdswoman tells him the herders have kept the days of the crossing longer than any living memory can number, and ask no more of it than that.

links.label: Same place
links.title: The crossing days of the panthers

told_in.book: Of Carson an Làmh Seo
told_in.section: I. Of the Carters' Roads

events.title: Coinneach hears the carters' grumbling at An Leòmhann Buidhe
events.body: At the road-house of An Leòmhann Buidhe, Coinneach overhears a coal-carter complain that the northern galleries want two men to a face where one once sufficed, and begins, without deciding to, keeping a private count of how often the like is said to him on the road.

links.label: Same place
links.title: An Leòmhann Buidhe on the north road

told_in.book: Of Carson an Làmh Seo
told_in.section: I. Of the Carters' Roads

events.title: Coinneach speaks with the teachers at Muileann chiar
events.body: In the sacred wood of Flidais at Muileann chiar, Coinneach tells the schools' elder teachers what he has gathered on the roads. Beathag nic Ruairidh names it a half question asked a thousand times, and tells him the schools want a fixed ground where it may be argued whole.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The house of disputation at Dùn thais

told_in.book: Of Carson an Làmh Seo
told_in.section: II. Of the Grove at Muileann chiar

events.title: Coinneach walks the bounds of the schools' wood
events.body: Coinneach walks the boundary stones of the sacred wood at Muileann chiar alone, as the schools' teachers do once in a lifetime, and comes out of it resolved to build a fixed house for the question he has carried, rather than carry it hearth to hearth any longer.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The house of disputation at Dùn thais

told_in.book: Of Carson an Làmh Seo
told_in.section: II. Of the Grove at Muileann chiar

events.title: The house of disputation at Dùn thais
events.body: Coinneach mac Mhàrtainn, a druid of the schools of Flidais, lady of the deer, founds a house of disputation at Dùn thais, where the old question of the schools, Carson an làmh seo?, why the vein answers some hands and not others, is argued by rule. Pupils come from as far as Caol bheag.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Coinneach speaks with the teachers at Muileann chiar

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Coinneach walks the bounds of the schools' wood

links.label: Same place
links.title: Taigh na Deasbaid raised at Dùn thais

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Pupils come from Caol bheag

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag nic Ruairidh visits the finished house

events.title: Taigh na Deasbaid raised at Dùn thais
events.body: Coinneach mac Mhàrtainn raises a hall of stone and turf at Dùn thais, Taigh na Deasbaid, and has the schools' old question, Carson an làmh seo?, cut into its lintel before the roof is finished. A rule is set: a question, once put, is argued a full year before any answer is given from the master's chair.

links.label: Same place
links.title: The house of disputation at Dùn thais

told_in.book: Of Carson an Làmh Seo
told_in.section: III. Of the House Raised at Dùn thais

events.title: Pupils come from Caol bheag
events.body: Word of the house at Dùn thais reaches the coast, and pupils begin walking three days from Caol bheag to sit its benches, sent by parents who have heard, by trader and carter, that a hard question is argued there properly. Among them is a fisherman's son, Aonghas mac Nèill, who stays to keep the house's register.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The house of disputation at Dùn thais

told_in.book: Of Carson an Làmh Seo
told_in.section: III. Of the House Raised at Dùn thais

events.title: Beathag nic Ruairidh visits the finished house
events.body: Beathag nic Ruairidh comes down from the grove of Muileann chiar to see the house Coinneach has built, walks its length in silence, and tells him afterward that the ground he has raised is fixed and patient enough, and asks only how long he means to let it argue safe things before he sets it the one question it was truly raised for.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The house of disputation at Dùn thais

told_in.book: Of Carson an Làmh Seo
told_in.section: III. Of the House Raised at Dùn thais

events.title: Birth of Uisdean mac Uisdein
events.body: A son, named Uisdean for his father, is born at Cathair dhearg to Uisdean mac Dhùghaill, then two-and-fifty years old and still waiting on his mother's long reign.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Death of Queen Sìleas

told_in.book: Of Carson an Làmh Seo
told_in.section: V. Of the Queen's Death and the Road Home

events.title: Coinneach's question
events.body: In open disputation Coinneach mac Mhàrtainn asks whether the hands that went with the fleet were those the vein answered best, and whether it now answers fewer. The seven houses forbid the question at their own tables; it is the first time they forbid a question and not a deed.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Coinneach asks the forbidden question

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The houses' ban carried to their tables

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: Coinneach walks home from the ban

events.title: Baile Mòr mhòr grows
events.body: After a run of poor seasons Baile Mòr mhòr on the northern plain takes in families from the upland farms and doubles within a generation. Its reeve divides the common grazing anew.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The reeve divides the grazing at Baile Mòr mhòr anew

events.title: Death of Queen Sìleas
events.body: Queen Sìleas nic Fhearchair dies at Cathair dhearg after a reign of more than fifty years. Her son Uisdean mac Dhùghaill is crowned.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Birth of Uisdean mac Dhùghaill

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of Uisdean mac Uisdein

links.label: Same place
links.title: Death of Queen Sìleas nic Fhearchair

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Uisdean mac Dhùghaill crowned

events.title: Coinneach asks the forbidden question
events.body: Before a full hall at Dùn thais, Coinneach mac Mhàrtainn asks at last whether the hands that went with the fleet were those the vein answered best, and whether it answers fewer now. No one on the benches answers him, and he sets the question, unanswered, into the house's register.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Coinneach's question

told_in.book: Of Carson an Làmh Seo
told_in.section: IV. Of the Open Disputation

events.title: The houses' ban carried to their tables
events.body: Word of Coinneach's question travels shire to shire until it has reached every one of the seven custodian houses, and each in its own hall forbids the question at its own table: the first time the seven have forbidden a question rather than a deed.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Coinneach's question

told_in.book: Of Carson an Làmh Seo
told_in.section: IV. Of the Open Disputation

events.title: The reeve divides the grazing at Baile Mòr mhòr anew
events.body: After a run of poor upland seasons, Baile Mòr mhòr has taken in so many families from the failing farms that the town has all but doubled, and its reeve marks out shares of the common grazing for households that never held a share of it before.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Baile Mòr mhòr grows

told_in.book: Of Carson an Làmh Seo
told_in.section: V. Of the Queen's Death and the Road Home

events.title: Death of Queen Sìleas nic Fhearchair
events.body: Queen Sìleas nic Fhearchair dies at Cathair dhearg, one-and-eighty years old, in An Talla Dearg where she had reigned longer than any ruler before her, a reign of six-and-sixty years begun when she was crowned at fifteen, too young by the houses' own custom to take the crown at once.

links.label: Same place
links.title: Death of Queen Sìleas

told_in.book: Of Carson an Làmh Seo
told_in.section: V. Of the Queen's Death and the Road Home

events.title: Uisdean mac Dhùghaill crowned
events.body: Uisdean mac Dhùghaill, Sìleas's son, no young man himself by then, is crowned at Cathair dhearg in his mother's place before the season turns. The crown's scribes set his crowning and her death on the same board, one line after the other, as though the two were a single piece of news.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Queen Sìleas

told_in.book: Of Carson an Làmh Seo
told_in.section: V. Of the Queen's Death and the Road Home

events.title: Coinneach walks home from the ban
events.body: Learning how Na Seachd Taighean have answered his question with a wider silence than his own, Coinneach mac Mhàrtainn walks the carters' road out from Dùn thais alone into the dark, and tells no pupil, then or after, what he has thought on the road.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: Coinneach's question

told_in.book: Of Carson an Làmh Seo
told_in.section: IV. Of the Open Disputation

events.title: Iain mac Ùisdein set to his father's toll
events.body: A boy of Drochaid Ros fhionn is set to sit the bridge with the tally-stick and learn his letters between carts, the office his father and grandfather held before him over the stone crossing above Ros fhionn.

told_in.book: Of Salt and the Listing Hull
told_in.section: II. Of the Bridge-Keeper's Boyhood and the Springs on the Flats

events.title: A reeve turns back from the pastures of Doire uaine before dark
events.body: A reeve sent from the shire seat to argue the shepherds of Doire uaine out of their custom of lighting no fires on the high pastures comes down again before dark the same day, and never returns to press the argument.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Hollow Man spoken of again

told_in.book: Of Salt and the Listing Hull
told_in.section: VI. Of the Hollow Man, a King's End, and the Fish of Àth fhiadhaich

events.title: The deep hull that would not float true
events.body: A merchant of Inis àrsaidh has a deep-keeled hull built for the long coast run eastward. The wrights no longer remember how Alasdair Saor scarfed his keels; the hull lists so badly at launch that it is broken up for timber.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ruairidh mac Artair's deep hull built at Inis àrsaidh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The hull that would not ride true

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Coll of Inis àrsaidh on the lost scarfing

events.title: Ruairidh mac Artair's deep hull built at Inis àrsaidh
events.body: A merchant of Inis àrsaidh pays wrights to lay a deep-keeled hull for the long coast run, in the manner remembered of the fleet's own building. No wright of the day still holds the old scarfing of the keel timbers that let those hulls flex to a sea.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The deep hull that would not float true

told_in.book: Of Salt and the Listing Hull
told_in.section: I. Of the Hull that Would Not Ride True

events.title: The hull that would not ride true
events.body: Ruairidh's hull lists at launch past any righting and is broken up for timber within the fortnight; none of the old builders' lore of the keel's joinery survives among the wrights who raised her. No one is hurt in the breaking-up.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The deep hull that would not float true

told_in.book: Of Salt and the Listing Hull
told_in.section: I. Of the Hull that Would Not Ride True

events.title: Coll of Inis àrsaidh on the lost scarfing
events.body: Coll, the oldest wright at Inis àrsaidh, looks over Ruairidh mac Artair's listing hull and says that no wright now living holds the old joinery of the keel that let the fleet's hulls flex to a sea; nobody has asked for it in three hundred years.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The deep hull that would not float true

told_in.book: Of Salt and the Listing Hull
told_in.section: I. Of the Hull that Would Not Ride True

events.title: Brine springs found on the flats above Ros fhionn
events.body: A farmer digging a drainage ditch above Ros fhionn strikes warm water that tastes of salt. Within a season the district's own folk have laid out shallow pans on the flats to catch the brine.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Salt pans at Ros fhionn

told_in.book: Of Salt and the Listing Hull
told_in.section: II. Of the Bridge-Keeper's Boyhood and the Springs on the Flats

events.title: Death of Uisdean mac Dhùghaill
events.body: Uisdean mac Dhùghaill dies at Cathair dhearg in his two-and-eightieth year, and his son Uisdean mac Uisdein, already thirty, is crowned without dispute. The tidings reach the northern flats by a rider bound for the shire seat.

told_in.book: Of Salt and the Listing Hull
told_in.section: III. Of a King's Death Far to the South and a Cloth Worn Nearer Home

events.title: Salt pans at Ros fhionn
events.body: The river town of Ros fhionn in the north-east lays out salt pans at the brine springs on its river flats and sends salt inland over Drochaid Ros fhionn. Within a generation Ros fhionn salt is the common measure of worth in the north-eastern shires.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Brine springs found on the flats above Ros fhionn

events.title: The wool of Baile gharbh
events.body: The weavers of Baile gharbh make a heavy undyed cloth that sheds rain, and it becomes the common cloak of the north-east. In this cloth the white sorrow is kept.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile gharbh's rain-cloth worn for mourning in the north-east

events.title: Baile gharbh's rain-cloth worn for mourning in the north-east
events.body: The heavy undyed cloth of Baile gharbh, already the common rain-cloak of the north-east, becomes the district's own cloth of mourning, worn plain and undyed through a household's season of loss as the whole island once wore an Tùrsa Geal.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The wool of Baile gharbh

told_in.book: Of Salt and the Listing Hull
told_in.section: III. Of a King's Death Far to the South and a Cloth Worn Nearer Home

events.title: Salt over Drochaid Ros fhionn
events.body: So many salt carts cross Drochaid Ros fhionn that the bridge-keeper is granted a handful from each load. His salt-box is said to hold more than some villages' granaries.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The bridge-keeper granted a handful from every load

events.title: The bridge-keeper granted a handful from every load
events.body: The shire seat grants the keeper of Drochaid Ros fhionn a handful of salt from every load crossing the bridge, in place of any other toll. Iain mac Ùisdein keeps the due honestly and becomes known along the road for it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Salt over Drochaid Ros fhionn

told_in.book: Of Salt and the Listing Hull
told_in.section: IV. Of the Handful from Each Load

events.title: Birth of Aonghas mac Uisdein
events.body: A son, Aonghas, is born at Cathair dhearg to Uisdean mac Uisdein in the twentieth year of his reign, when the king is fifty years old.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Aonghas mac Uisdein crowned

told_in.book: Of Salt and the Listing Hull
told_in.section: III. Of a King's Death Far to the South and a Cloth Worn Nearer Home

events.title: The bridge-keeper's salt-box
events.body: Iain mac Ùisdein builds an iron-bound oak box beside his stool to hold his due of salt. It fills faster than any box on that road was thought able to fill, and carters along the way say it holds more against a hard winter than some whole villages.

told_in.book: Of Salt and the Listing Hull
told_in.section: IV. Of the Handful from Each Load

events.title: The wells crack at Cill ghlas
events.body: An earth tremor in the hills about Cill ghlas cracks three wells and brings down a byre. The custodians of the vein-house note it, and note that the galleries were untouched.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The wells crack at Cill ghlas

events.title: The wells crack at Cill ghlas
events.body: An earth tremor cracks three wells and brings down a byre at Cill ghlas. The custodians of Taigh na Fèithe send men into the galleries below and find the deep workings untouched, though the diggers speak among themselves of feeling the shaking reach them under the hill.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The wells crack at Cill ghlas

told_in.book: Of Salt and the Listing Hull
told_in.section: V. Of the Wells that Cracked at Cill ghlas

events.title: Taigh na Fèithe offers stone for Cill ghlas's byre
events.body: The custodians of Taigh na Fèithe offer stone from their own surplus to rebuild the byre brought down at Cill ghlas, a kindness the village does not forget.

told_in.book: Of Salt and the Listing Hull
told_in.section: V. Of the Wells that Cracked at Cill ghlas

events.title: Mòr nic Nèill made tutor to the king's son
events.body: Mòr nic Nèill is set over the young Aonghas mac Uisdein to teach him his letters as a child, the first time any heir to An Talla Dearg has been given a tutor for the purpose rather than left to pick up his letters between other business.

told_in.book: Of Salt and the Listing Hull
told_in.section: VI. Of the Hollow Man, a King's End, and the Fish of Àth fhiadhaich

events.title: The Hollow Man spoken of again
events.body: The shepherds of the Doire uaine hills will light no fires on the high pastures, for the old inscriptions of Marbh-bheò Doire uaine. A reeve sent from Muileann chiar to make them see sense does not stay the night.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A reeve turns back from the pastures of Doire uaine before dark

events.title: Aonghas mac Uisdein crowned
events.body: Uisdean mac Uisdein dies, the son of Uisdean mac Dhùghaill and king after him, and his own son Aonghas mac Uisdein is crowned at Cathair dhearg, a young man of twenty-two. Aonghas is the first king to learn his letters as a child.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of Aonghas mac Uisdein

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Death of Uisdean mac Uisdein and the crowning of Aonghas

events.title: Àth fhiadhaich salt fish
events.body: Àth fhiadhaich begins to salt its catch with Ros fhionn salt and send it inland to the mining towns. From this time the mining shires eat salt fish in the lean season.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Àth fhiadhaich turns to Ros fhionn salt

events.title: Death of Uisdean mac Uisdein and the crowning of Aonghas
events.body: Uisdean mac Uisdein dies at two-and-seventy after two-and-forty years in the hall. His son Aonghas, two-and-twenty and taught his letters as a child, is crowned at Cathair dhearg with less dispute than any crowning in living memory.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Aonghas mac Uisdein crowned

told_in.book: Of Salt and the Listing Hull
told_in.section: VI. Of the Hollow Man, a King's End, and the Fish of Àth fhiadhaich

events.title: Àth fhiadhaich turns to Ros fhionn salt
events.body: The fishing town of Àth fhiadhaich, having lost catch to poor curing, begins sending carts north for Ros fhionn salt. From this year the mining shires to the south eat their salt fish cured with salt carried over Drochaid Ros fhionn.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Àth fhiadhaich salt fish

told_in.book: Of Salt and the Listing Hull
told_in.section: VI. Of the Hollow Man, a King's End, and the Fish of Àth fhiadhaich

events.title: Birth of Aonghas Òg
events.body: A son, named Aonghas for his father, is born at Cathair dhearg to King Aonghas mac Uisdein, eight-and-twenty years old and six years crowned.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Death of King Aonghas

told_in.book: Of the Stone that Cries Out and the Two Horses
told_in.section: VI. Of the Two Horses

events.title: An old watching family questions Dòmhnall mac Ailein's right to name the stone
events.body: One of the families who have kept watch on the wolf-stone at Inis thais for generations sends its eldest to ask a net-maker preaching on the strand what right he has to put a new name on their old duty. He answers that he claims no watch of his own and has only said aloud what the family's own hands have been doing unnamed for years.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Clach first preached at Inis thais

told_in.book: Of the Stone that Cries Out and the Two Horses
told_in.section: I. Of the Net-Maker of Inis thais

events.title: Dòmhnall mac Ailein's first preaching on the strand
events.body: A net-maker of Inis thais, thirty-five years old, begins telling the men who mend nets beside him that the town's old wolf-stone is Lia Fàil, and that its watching families are an Fhianna, sworn to keep the whole island as a wolf keeps its range. His hearers grow through the year into the first gathering of Òrd na Cloiche at Inis thais.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Clach first preached at Inis thais

told_in.book: Of the Stone that Cries Out and the Two Horses
told_in.section: I. Of the Net-Maker of Inis thais

events.title: Clach first preached at Inis thais
events.body: Dòmhnall mac Ailein, a net-maker of Inis thais, where the wolf-sworn's stone Clach stands, preaches that the stone is Lia Fàil, which cries out under the rightful king, and that its sworn guards are the Fianna, who keep the island as a wolf keeps its range. His hearers are the first congregation of Òrd na Cloiche, the order of the Stone.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: An old watching family questions Dòmhnall mac Ailein's right to name the stone

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Dòmhnall mac Ailein's first preaching on the strand

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: The naming of Lia Fàil carried inland by a hide-trader

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Death of Dòmhnall mac Ailein

events.title: A shipmaster of Inis thais sails north for slate
events.body: Beathag nic Raoghnaill, a shipmaster who has carried wool and hides along the southern coast for twenty years, offers to fetch roofing slate for the wolf-stone's new hall herself rather than trust the errand to another. She returns a season later with a hull low under northern slate.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The wolf-house at Inis thais

told_in.book: Of the Stone that Cries Out and the Two Horses
told_in.section: II. Of the Wolf-House Roofed with Slate

events.title: Slate brought by sea for the temple at Inis thais
events.body: The northern slate Beathag nic Raoghnaill brought south is laid over the wolf-stone's new hall, the first roof on that coast built to outlast its own builder. The town remarks as much on the roof's cost as on its wonder.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The wolf-house at Inis thais

told_in.book: Of the Stone that Cries Out and the Two Horses
told_in.section: II. Of the Wolf-House Roofed with Slate

events.title: The wolf-house at Inis thais
events.body: The followers of Dòmhnall mac Ailein raise at Inis thais the first temple on the island to Lia Fàil by name. It is roofed with slate brought by sea from the north.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A shipmaster of Inis thais sails north for slate

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Slate brought by sea for the temple at Inis thais

events.title: The tide-horn of the wolf-stone shrine
events.body: An Fhianna at Inis thais take up a horn blown at every turn of the tide, its blowing passed by lot among the watching households. Within a few years the town sets its morning's business by the horn without a thought for what it was first blown to mark.

told_in.book: Of the Stone that Cries Out and the Two Horses
told_in.section: II. Of the Wolf-House Roofed with Slate

events.title: The naming of Lia Fàil carried inland by a hide-trader
events.body: A fisherman of Inis thais who has heard Dòmhnall mac Ailein twice repeats the naming of Lia Fàil to three inland villages while selling hides that winter, none of which he visits again. The teaching spreads in threads too small to trace to their source.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: Clach first preached at Inis thais

told_in.book: Of the Stone that Cries Out and the Two Horses
told_in.section: II. Of the Wolf-House Roofed with Slate

events.title: Òrd an t-Seabhaig and an Fhianna claim the same feast day at Caol leathan
events.body: The priests of Òrd an t-Seabhaig and an Fhianna both come to the harbour shrine at Caol leathan for the same morning's hours, Òrd an t-Seabhaig's reckoning and Òrd na Cloiche's vigil falling that year on the same day. Neither will give way.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Hawk and wolf at Caol leathan

told_in.book: Of the Stone that Cries Out and the Two Horses
told_in.section: III. Of the Harbour Shrine at Caol leathan

events.title: Hawk and wolf at Caol leathan
events.body: The priests of the Hawk and the Fianna of the Stone both claim the harbour shrine at Caol leathan. The king's reeve divides its days between them, as the sacred woods were divided in the Holy Age, and the division holds.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Òrd an t-Seabhaig and an Fhianna claim the same feast day at Caol leathan

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Murchadh mac Ailpein divides the shrine's days

events.title: Murchadh mac Ailpein divides the shrine's days
events.body: The king's reeve at Caol leathan, Murchadh mac Ailpein, halves the harbour shrine's hours between Òrd an t-Seabhaig and an Fhianna, as the sacred woods of an older age were once divided, and nails the division on a strip of hide to the shrine door.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Hawk and wolf at Caol leathan

told_in.book: Of the Stone that Cries Out and the Two Horses
told_in.section: III. Of the Harbour Shrine at Caol leathan

events.title: The market inside the new gate
events.body: Seann Skell on the Hawk bay is walled, and a market is granted inside the new landward gate, where amber, whale-oil, honey and the sheep of the northern moors are sold. The amber-workers of the bay swear to sell no rough amber outside the walls.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailig an Òir forfeits a season's amber

events.title: Birth of Iain mac Aonghais
events.body: A son, Iain, is born at Cathair dhearg to Aonghas Òg, the king's heir, then five-and-thirty years old; the old king, sixty-three, sees his grandson named at the yoke-poles of Macha's rite.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Tormod Bàn crowned

told_in.book: Of the Stone that Cries Out and the Two Horses
told_in.section: VI. Of the Two Horses

events.title: Ailig an Òir forfeits a season's amber
events.body: An amber-worker of Seann Skell on Bàgh an t-Seabhaig is caught selling rough amber outside the new walls against his own guild's oath, and is made by that guild to forfeit the whole season's gathering to the market fund rather than face the crown's reeve.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The market inside the new gate

told_in.book: Of the Stone that Cries Out and the Two Horses
