told_in.section: IV. Of Seann Skell Walled and the Market at the New Gate

events.title: Death of Dòmhnall mac Ailein
events.body: Dòmhnall mac Ailein dies at Inis thais in his seventieth year, having taught on the strand five-and-thirty years without ever taking up an office in the order his hearers named after his teaching. An Fhianna carry him to the shrine and set him before it, not within it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Clach first preached at Inis thais

told_in.book: Of the Stone that Cries Out and the Two Horses
told_in.section: V. Of Dòmhnall's Death

events.title: Macha at court
events.body: King Aonghas takes up the wood-watchers' rite of Macha, which keeps the two horses of one chariot, foaled on one night, Liath Macha the grey and Dubh Sainglenn the black: two horses, one yoke, light and dark two powers in balance, and the vein belonging to both. The court follows him, and Òrd Mhacha, the order of Macha, becomes the order of Cathair dhearg and the crown.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: King Aonghas recalls his father's teaching on the two horses

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A councillor warns Aonghas against Òrd Mhacha' rite

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Half An Talla Dearg's household takes up the rite of Macha

links.label: Leads to
links.title: King Aonghas returns to the yoke a second year

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Death of King Aonghas mac Uisdein

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Aonghas Òg crowned at fifty

events.title: King Aonghas recalls his father's teaching on the two horses
events.body: Before he takes up Òrd Mhacha' rite himself, King Aonghas mac Uisdein recalls being told as a boy that one horse pulling alone draws a chariot only in a circle, and that it takes two, pulling together and never quite agreeing, to pull it straight.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Macha at court

told_in.book: Of the Stone that Cries Out and the Two Horses
told_in.section: VI. Of the Two Horses

events.title: A councillor warns Aonghas against Òrd Mhacha' rite
events.body: An old councillor of An Talla Dearg warns King Aonghas that a crown seen at a moor-custom may be asked by Na Seachd Taighean why it will not be seen at theirs. Aonghas answers that any house is free to come and stand at a yoke-pole itself.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Macha at court

told_in.book: Of the Stone that Cries Out and the Two Horses
told_in.section: VI. Of the Two Horses

events.title: Half An Talla Dearg's household takes up the rite of Macha
events.body: Within a year of King Aonghas standing at the yoke-pole of Òrd Mhacha' rite, half his own household has taken it up beside him, and Òrd Mhacha becomes from that year the order of Cathair dhearg without a quarrel fought over it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Macha at court

told_in.book: Of the Stone that Cries Out and the Two Horses
told_in.section: VI. Of the Two Horses

events.title: A quarryman's household first roofs in slate at Tobar dhearg
events.body: A family burned out in the fire at Tobar dhearg, a quarryman among them, is the first in the village to roof again in slate rather than thatch, judging that a man who cuts the stone has less excuse than his neighbours to sleep under straw.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fire at Tobar dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Stone that Cries Out and the Two Horses
told_in.section: VII. Of the Fire at Tobar dhearg

events.title: The crown sends grain south after the fire at Tobar dhearg
events.body: King Aonghas sends what the crown's granaries can spare south to Tobar dhearg before the winter closes the roads, the village having lost most of its stores along with its roofs.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fire at Tobar dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Stone that Cries Out and the Two Horses
told_in.section: VII. Of the Fire at Tobar dhearg

events.title: King Aonghas returns to the yoke a second year
events.body: King Aonghas rides out to Òrd Mhacha' rite a second spring running, judging that a thing done once by a king and not again is no rite at all, and stands again with a hand on each yoke-pole among the grey horse and the black.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Macha at court

told_in.book: Of the Stone that Cries Out and the Two Horses
told_in.section: VII. Of the Fire at Tobar dhearg

events.title: Fire at Tobar dhearg
events.body: Fire runs through the thatch of Tobar dhearg and burns most of the village. It is rebuilt with slate from the quarries nearby, and is known thereafter for its slate roofs.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A quarryman's household first roofs in slate at Tobar dhearg

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The crown sends grain south after the fire at Tobar dhearg

events.title: Death of King Aonghas mac Uisdein
events.body: King Aonghas mac Uisdein dies at Cathair dhearg in his seventy-eighth year, after six-and-fifty years crowned, having set Òrd Mhacha' rite of Macha as the crown's own custom. Leabhar a' Chùraim gives him one line: the name, the year, and no more.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Macha at court

told_in.book: Of the Burned Tracts
told_in.section: VI. Of Three Kings in a Single Generation

events.title: Aonghas Òg crowned at fifty
events.body: Aonghas Òg mac Aonghais is crowned at Cathair dhearg the same season his father dies, fifty years old and no young man, for all his name.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Macha at court

told_in.book: Of the Burned Tracts
told_in.section: VI. Of Three Kings in a Single Generation

events.title: Eilidh Dhubh begins to teach at Doire chiar
events.body: Eilidh nic Iain, taught in secret by her grandmother, begins to say aloud at Doire chiar the old teaching that the vein answers labour and not birth. She sets it down in a hand her mother taught her, and pupils begin to copy it for households too far off to hear her speak.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh Dhubh's tracts

told_in.book: Of the Burned Tracts
told_in.section: I. Of the Woman Who Taught at Doire chiar

events.title: Birth of Tormod Bàn
events.body: A son, Tormod, fair-haired from the cradle and so called Tormod Bàn, is born at Cathair dhearg to Iain mac Aonghais, five-and-twenty years old, in the tenth year of his grandfather Aonghas Òg's reign.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Tormod Bàn crowned

told_in.book: Of the Burned Tracts
told_in.section: VII. Of the Second Son

events.title: Macha's priests in Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag
events.body: The custody of Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag, shared since the Holy Age, passes by royal grant to the priests of Macha. The other claimants leave the wood without contest. Why is not told.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Macha's priests granted Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag

events.title: Macha's priests granted Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag
events.body: The custody of Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag, held in common since An Aois Naomh, passes by royal grant to the priests of Macha alone. The other claimants withdraw from the wood the same season without contest; why they go so quietly is not told.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Macha's priests in Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag

told_in.book: Of the Burned Tracts
told_in.section: IV. Of the Wood and the Road

events.title: Taigh na Fèithe orders every copy of the tracts given up
events.body: Word of Eilidh Dhubh's tracts reaches the custodians' galleries at Muileann dhearg, and Taigh na Fèithe orders every copy brought in and given up, promising no penalty to any household that surrenders one freely before the season's end.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The tracts burned at Muileann dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Burned Tracts
told_in.section: III. Of the Order from Muileann dhearg

events.title: Some hundred tracts burned in Taigh na Fèithe yard
events.body: Carriers gather some hundred hides and boards of Eilidh Dhubh's tracts from households across the north-east and burn them in Taigh na Fèithe yard at Muileann dhearg before the gathered custodians. Eilidh walks from Doire chiar to see it done, and says nothing.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The tracts burned at Muileann dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Burned Tracts
told_in.section: III. Of the Order from Muileann dhearg

events.title: A harvest gathering at Muileann chiar hears the tracts read
events.body: Coinneach Odhar, taught his letters by Eilidh Dhubh to carry her teaching where she will not travel, reads the tracts aloud for the first time at a harvest gathering near Muileann chiar. Not every household takes to it easily, and a farmer's wife elsewhere warns that the teaching could get colliers killed.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh Dhubh's tracts

told_in.book: Of the Burned Tracts
told_in.section: II. Of the Reading at Harvest

events.title: The druid schools keep Coille Naomh Muileann chiar
events.body: The druids of the schools take the keeping of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar, the wood of Flidais's white stag, and walk its bounds each year. The walk becomes the one open rite of the schools.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Scoiltean nan Draoidhean take up the walk of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar

events.title: Scoiltean nan Draoidhean take up the walk of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar
events.body: Scoiltean nan Draoidhean, holding no ground of their own since An Aois Naomh, take up the yearly keeping of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar at Muileann chiar, walking its bounds in a procession that grows within a decade into the one rite the schools still keep open to any who will walk with them.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The druid schools keep Coille Naomh Muileann chiar

told_in.book: Of the Burned Tracts
told_in.section: IV. Of the Wood and the Road

events.title: The drovers of Àth chiar
events.body: Drovers of Àth chiar begin to drive cattle each year over the eastern hills to the mining towns. Theirs are the first roads on the island marked with cairns.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The drovers of Àth chiar raise the first cairns

events.title: Eilidh Dhubh's tracts
events.body: At Doire chiar Eilidh nic Iain, called Eilidh Dhubh, wakes again the teaching of the rival school of the Holy Age, that the vein answers labour and not birth, and sets it out in tracts that her pupils copy. The tracts are read aloud at harvest gatherings across the north-east.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Eilidh Dhubh begins to teach at Doire chiar

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A harvest gathering at Muileann chiar hears the tracts read

events.title: The tracts burned at Muileann dhearg
events.body: The vein-house commands every copy of Eilidh Dhubh's tracts brought to Muileann dhearg and burned, and some hundred are given up. Eilidh is not punished. She dies at Doire chiar, still teaching.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Taigh na Fèithe orders every copy of the tracts given up

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Some hundred tracts burned in Taigh na Fèithe yard

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A hidden copy of the tracts kept at Doire chiar

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Death of Eilidh Dhubh

events.title: Death of King Aonghas
events.body: King Aonghas Òg, son of Aonghas mac Uisdein and crowned after him, dies at Cathair dhearg and is buried by the rite of Macha, the first king so buried. His son Iain mac Aonghais is crowned.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of Aonghas Òg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: King Aonghas Òg buried by the rite of Macha

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain mac Aonghais crowned at nine-and-forty

events.title: King Aonghas Òg buried by the rite of Macha
events.body: King Aonghas Òg dies in the winter of his eighty-fourth year and is carried to his grave at Cathair dhearg by Òrd Mhacha' rite of Macha, the first king of the line so buried. His household stands at the yoke-poles of the two horses he rode out to see brought up together every spring of his reign.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of King Aonghas

told_in.book: Of the Burned Tracts
told_in.section: VI. Of Three Kings in a Single Generation

events.title: The drovers of Àth chiar raise the first cairns
events.body: The drovers who drive cattle each year from Àth chiar over the eastern hills to the mining towns begin marking their road with a cairn at every day's stage, the first roads on the island so marked, so that a beast lost in mist or a driver new to the trade may find the way again unasked.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The drovers of Àth chiar

told_in.book: Of the Burned Tracts
told_in.section: IV. Of the Wood and the Road

events.title: Iain mac Aonghais crowned at nine-and-forty
events.body: Iain mac Aonghais is crowned at Cathair dhearg after his father Aonghas Òg is carried to his grave by Macha's rite, nine-and-forty years old, with three sons living.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of King Aonghas

told_in.book: Of the Burned Tracts
told_in.section: VI. Of Three Kings in a Single Generation

events.title: A hidden copy of the tracts kept at Doire chiar
events.body: A single hide of the tracts, in Eilidh Dhubh's mother's own hand, is kept whole in a hollow beam of Eilidh's house, given to no household but her own kin's. Eilidh shows it to no one outside her family, judging it kept for her mother's sake more than the country's.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The tracts burned at Muileann dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Burned Tracts
told_in.section: V. Of the Copy Kept at Doire chiar

events.title: Birth of Dùghall, Iain mac Aonghais's son by his second wife
events.body: King Iain mac Aonghais, his first wife some years dead, takes a second wife who bears him a third son, Dùghall, the first of his three sons born at An Talla Dearg itself under a crown his father already wears.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod Bàn crowned

told_in.book: Of the Burned Tracts
told_in.section: VII. Of the Second Son

events.title: Tormod Bàn crowned
events.body: Iain mac Aonghais dies after a short reign, and his son Tormod mac Iain, called Tormod Bàn for his white hair, is crowned at Cathair dhearg. The houses swear to him without dispute.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of Iain mac Aonghais

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of Tormod Bàn

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Birth of Dùghall, Iain mac Aonghais's son by his second wife

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Death of King Iain mac Aonghais

events.title: Death of King Iain mac Aonghais
events.body: King Iain mac Aonghais dies at Cathair dhearg at one-and-sixty, twelve years crowned, the third king An Talla Dearg has buried in a single generation. His second son Aonghas, nineteen, stands a pace back from the hall's centre at his brother Tormod's crowning.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tormod Bàn crowned

told_in.book: Of the Burned Tracts
told_in.section: VII. Of the Second Son

events.title: Death of Eilidh Dhubh
events.body: Eilidh nic Iain, Eilidh Dhubh, dies at Doire chiar in her seventy-fifth year, still teaching within the hour of her death. Her pupils raise no stone over her, and Coinneach Odhar reads the tracts aloud at her graveside from the copy he has carried thirty years.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The tracts burned at Muileann dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Burned Tracts
told_in.section: V. Of the Copy Kept at Doire chiar

events.title: Winter at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr
events.body: An Taigh-seinnse Mòr on the central mining road becomes the house where the ox-teams of the mountain wait out the worst of the snow. Its keeper, Iain mac Mhurchaidh, builds them a second byre and keeps a book of the teams that lodged.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain mac Mhurchaidh raises a second byre at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr

events.title: Iain mac Mhurchaidh raises a second byre at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr
events.body: Iain mac Mhurchaidh, keeper of the road-house at the halfway stage of the central mining road, raises a second byre against the growing traffic of the ox-teams and begins a careful book of every team that lodges there through the mountain snows.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Winter at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr

told_in.book: Of the Burned Tracts
told_in.section: VIII. Of the Byre at the Halfway Stage

events.title: The bell-founders of Muileann naomh
events.body: A family of Muileann naomh casts the first bronze bell on Dia-thìr to hang in a hawk-house. It cracks in its first frost; the second holds.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The second bell of Muileann naomh holds

events.title: The second bell of Muileann naomh holds
events.body: After the first bell cast for the hawk-house at Muileann naomh cracks in its first frost, the founders cast a second, thicker at the waist, and it holds, ringing thereafter at every measured burning kept at the house and at every turn of the coast's own reckoning of the year besides.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The bell-founders of Muileann naomh

told_in.book: Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn
told_in.section: I. Of the Bell at Muileann naomh

events.title: An Gàire Dubh
events.body: A storm named in the south-coast rolls An Gàire Dubh, the Black Laugh, drives the sea over the waterfront of Cuan dhearg and spoils the season's salt fish. The town is built again a street further from the shore.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod Bàn hears the tidings of An Gàire Dubh standing

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king sends grain south unasked

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cuan dhearg rebuilds a street back from the shore

links.label: Leads to
links.title: King Tormod visits Cuan dhearg's new street

events.title: Tormod Bàn hears the tidings of An Gàire Dubh standing
events.body: Word of the sea driven over the waterfront of Cuan dhearg reaches An Talla Dearg nine days late by a rider who has ridden two horses to death. King Tormod Bàn, nine-and-fifty, hears it standing, as his scribes note he does only when a report troubles him past sitting.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: An Gàire Dubh

told_in.book: Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn
told_in.section: II. Of An Gàire Dubh

events.title: The king sends grain south unasked
events.body: Before the roads close for the winter King Tormod Bàn sends grain south to Cuan dhearg, though its reeve has sent no asking, only the bare report of the water; the season's salt fish had spoiled on the racks below the town.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: An Gàire Dubh

told_in.book: Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn
told_in.section: II. Of An Gàire Dubh

events.title: Cuan dhearg rebuilds a street back from the shore
events.body: After An Gàire Dubh drowns its waterfront, Cuan dhearg of the red cliffs rebuilds a full street back from the old shoreline, on ground no telling the town keeps says the sea has ever reached, and the new street holds.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: An Gàire Dubh

told_in.book: Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn
told_in.section: II. Of An Gàire Dubh

events.title: King Tormod visits Cuan dhearg's new street
events.body: King Tormod Bàn rides to Cuan dhearg to see its rebuilt street, the one journey of his reign made, his own scribes note, for a storm's sake alone rather than for a war, a crowning or a rite the crown was bound to keep.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: An Gàire Dubh

told_in.book: Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn
told_in.section: II. Of An Gàire Dubh

events.title: A reciter of Clann na Ceiste says Clann a' Chlachair at a naming
events.body: At a naming among the wells of Tobar dhìreach, for a steward's son of the king's own household, the reciter Muireach mac Ailein says the line of An Clachair over the child rather than the long line of Somhairle that royal namings there have called on for generations.

told_in.book: Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn
told_in.section: III. Of the Naming at Tobar dhìreach

events.title: The hawk-house at Muileann naomh
events.body: Muileann naomh in the south becomes the southernmost house of the Hawk, and rings its bell at each measured burning. There the Hawk's teaching holds when it fades elsewhere in the south.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Muileann naomh draws pilgrims from further south

events.title: Birth of Catrìona nic Aonghais at Inis thais
events.body: A daughter, Catrìona, is born at Inis thais to Aonghas mac Iain, the king's brother, and his wife Mairead nic Ailein, the first child of that marriage to live past her own naming. King Tormod Bàn rides down himself to see her named.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The three claimants

told_in.book: Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn
told_in.section: IV. Of the Child at Inis thais

events.title: Muileann naomh draws pilgrims from further south
events.body: Word of the hawk-house at Muileann naomh, where the old teaching is still given whole and unsoftened, carries south along the coast, and pilgrims begin to come to it from towns further south than any hawk-house had drawn from before.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hawk-house at Muileann naomh

told_in.book: Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn
told_in.section: I. Of the Bell at Muileann naomh

events.title: Death of Aonghas mac Iain
events.body: Aonghas mac Iain, the king's brother, dies at Inis thais in his fifty-fourth year of a wasting sickness, King Tormod Bàn having ridden down to sit with him three days before the end. He is buried in the ground of that coast, at his own household's asking.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The three claimants

told_in.book: Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn
told_in.section: V. Of Aonghas mac Iain's Death

events.title: Mairead nic Ailein keeps her daughter from An Talla Dearg
events.body: Offered a place under the king's own roof for her widowed household, Mairead nic Ailein keeps her daughter Catrìona at Inis thais rather than raise her at Cathair dhearg, judging a fatherless girl better raised among neighbours than as a king's ward with an unnamed claim.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The three claimants

told_in.book: Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn
told_in.section: V. Of Aonghas mac Iain's Death

events.title: The king's sons drowned in Abhainn fhionn
events.body: Both sons of King Tormod Bàn drown when a ferry overturns on Abhainn fhionn in spate. The king has no other child.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Odhar cleared of blame for the ferry

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A new ferry ordered a mile upstream

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Odhar made keeper of the new crossing

events.title: Iain Odhar cleared of blame for the ferry
events.body: The ferryman Iain Odhar comes before the king's reeves to answer for the ferry's overturning, and is cleared: he judged the spate as he had judged the river a hundred times before, and no such flood had come down that crossing unwarned in his eleven years on the rope.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The king's sons drowned in Abhainn fhionn

told_in.book: Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn
told_in.section: VI. Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn

events.title: A new ferry ordered a mile upstream
events.body: King Tormod Bàn has the old ferry rope cut and burned and orders a second crossing built a mile upstream, where the ford-keepers judge the river safer in spate, and never crosses the Abhainn fhionn again without a rider sent ahead to test the current.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The king's sons drowned in Abhainn fhionn

told_in.book: Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn
told_in.section: VI. Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn

events.title: Iain Odhar made keeper of the new crossing
events.body: The king grants Iain Odhar a small holding above the new crossing, not as payment for the two lives the old ferry took, but as a keeper's fee, and the ferryman watches the new rope closely for the thirty years he has left to keep it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The king's sons drowned in Abhainn fhionn

told_in.book: Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn
told_in.section: VI. Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn

events.title: The three nearest the crown reckoned
events.body: In the fourth year after the ferry, the custodians of Taigh na Fèithe cease to reckon quietly who stands nearest the crown: Dùghall Garbh the king's half-brother, Catrìona nic Aonghais his niece, and Raghnall Ruadh of Clann Raghnaill.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The three claimants

told_in.book: Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn
told_in.section: VII. Of the Thirteen Years

events.title: Raghnall Ruadh made master of Taigh na Fèithe
events.body: The custodians of Taigh na Fèithe at Muileann dhearg choose Raghnall Ruadh, head of Clann Raghnaill, as master over two men of longer service, judging that Taigh na Fèithe, which may soon answer to no clear crown, had better answer to the steadiest hand at hand.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The three claimants

told_in.book: Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn
told_in.section: VII. Of the Thirteen Years

events.title: A councillor asks King Tormod to name an heir
events.body: An old councillor of An Talla Dearg asks King Tormod Bàn, seven years after the ferry, whether he means to name one of the three standing nearest the crown before age chooses in his place. The king answers that he will hold the crown himself while breath allows it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Death of Tormod Bàn

told_in.book: Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn
told_in.section: VII. Of the Thirteen Years

events.title: Death of Tormod Bàn
events.body: King Tormod Bàn dies at Cathair dhearg without naming an heir, and three claims are laid before the houses at once.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A councillor asks King Tormod to name an heir

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod Bàn's last order

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The houses hold the hall in common

events.title: Tormod Bàn's last order
events.body: Dying at Cathair dhearg at seven-and-eighty, one-and-fifty years crowned, King Tormod Bàn gives his last clear order to the scribe beside him: that the boundary dispute at Àth chiar, unsettled after three seasons, go to the custodians to finish.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Tormod Bàn

told_in.book: Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn
told_in.section: VIII. Of the King's Death and the Houses Divided

events.title: The houses hold the hall in common
events.body: Unable to agree on any one of the three claims laid before them, Na Seachd Taighean hold An Talla Dearg in common, the custodians sitting together in the crown's stead and keeping the kingdom's small business moving while the larger question of the crown stands unanswered.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Tormod Bàn

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The three claimants

told_in.book: Of the Ferry on the Abhainn fhionn
told_in.section: VIII. Of the King's Death and the Houses Divided

events.title: The three claimants
events.body: The crown is claimed by Catrìona nic Aonghais of Inis thais, niece of the late king; by Dùghall Garbh of Baile Mòr dhomhain, his half-brother; and by Raghnall Ruadh, head of Clann Raghnaill and master of the vein-house. The seven houses divide among them, and the War of the Three Claimants begins.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Birth of Catrìona nic Aonghais at Inis thais

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Death of Aonghas mac Iain

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Mairead nic Ailein keeps her daughter from An Talla Dearg

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The three nearest the crown reckoned

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Raghnall Ruadh made master of Taigh na Fèithe

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The houses hold the hall in common

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mairead nic Ruairidh bars the gate to all three

events.title: Mairead nic Ruairidh bars the gate to all three
events.body: The heralds of Catrìona nic Aonghais, Dùghall Garbh and Raghnall Ruadh come one after another to the western gate of Seann Warr, and its reeve Mairead nic Ruairidh gives each the same answer: the town will open to trade and shut to hosts until the houses agree which claim to answer.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seann Warr shuts its gates

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The three claimants

told_in.book: Of the Ford and the Fouled Wells
told_in.section: I. Of the Gates Shut Against All Three

events.title: Seann Warr shuts its gates
events.body: Seann Warr, the port nearest the capital on the west, shuts its gates to all three claimants and declares for none. Twice besieged in the war, it is taken by neither.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Mairead nic Ruairidh bars the gate to all three

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seann Warr's first siege

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seann Warr's second siege

events.title: Seann Warr's first siege
events.body: Dùghall Garbh sits before Seann Warr a fortnight, cutting the eastern road, but its salt-pans and brine springs feed the town through the siege. Mairead nic Ruairidh sells his own host bread at the market rate until his carters cost him more than the town is worth, and he withdraws.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seann Warr shuts its gates

told_in.book: Of the Ford and the Fouled Wells
told_in.section: II. Of the First Siege

events.title: The ford at Àth shean
events.body: The host of Dùghall Garbh meets that of Raghnall Ruadh at the ford of Àth shean and breaks it. The custody-book counts some three hundred dead, most of them drowned in the ford.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dùghall crosses the shallows by night

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Catrìona's answer to the ford

links.label: Answered by
links.title: Fearchar Ciar swears the ford broke on two days

events.title: Dùghall crosses the shallows by night
events.body: Guided by drovers who have used a hidden ford above Àth shean for forty years to move cattle untolled, Dùghall Garbh crosses his host in the dark and comes down on Raghnall Ruadh's camp from the landward side before dawn.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The ford at Àth shean

told_in.book: Of the Ford and the Fouled Wells
told_in.section: III. Of the Ford at Àth shean

events.title: Catrìona's answer to the ford
events.body: Hearing word of Raghnall's breaking at the ford, Catrìona nic Aonghais sends Dùghall Garbh an answer naming no alliance: Cathair dhomhain holds for him, not for her, and she will not thank him for taking it from under her siege lines.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The ford at Àth shean

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The siege of Cathair dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Ford and the Fouled Wells
told_in.section: III. Of the Ford at Àth shean

events.title: Coinneach mac Ailein's household flees Doire mhin
events.body: Woken by fire in the night, Coinneach mac Ailein carries his daughter Seònaid and the year's seed-corn out of the burning village of Doire mhin, while his wife brings the two younger children and the loosed cow finds its own way into the dark.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The burning of Doire mhin

told_in.book: Of the Ford and the Fouled Wells
told_in.section: IV. Of Doire mhin, and of the Child Seònaid

events.title: The burning of Doire mhin
events.body: Raghnall Ruadh's men in retreat burn the village of Doire mhin and its granary, to deny them to Dùghall. The villagers winter at Cathair mhòr on the charity of Macha's priests.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Coinneach mac Ailein's household flees Doire mhin

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Doire mhin folk at Cathair mhòr

events.title: The Doire mhin folk at Cathair mhòr
events.body: Forty-one burnt-out households of Doire mhin, walking six days south with what little they carried, are taken in at the temple of Macha in Cathair mhòr and fed through the winter on the temple's grain, without regard to whose claim they had favoured.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The burning of Doire mhin

told_in.book: Of the Ford and the Fouled Wells
told_in.section: IV. Of Doire mhin, and of the Child Seònaid

events.title: Seann Warr's second siege
events.body: Dùghall Garbh, better provisioned than before, sits a full month before Seann Warr. The town holds again, though the winter comes on hard behind the siege, until word reaches Dùghall that Catrìona has closed both gates of Cathair dhomhain, and he marches east.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seann Warr shuts its gates

told_in.book: Of the Ford and the Fouled Wells
told_in.section: V. Of the Second Siege

events.title: The water gate of Cathair dhomhain is closed
events.body: On the counsel of a harbour-master of her following, Catrìona nic Aonghais sends borrowed fishing coasters onto the loch by night to shut Cathair dhomhain's water gate as her lines already hold the land gate, and the siege begins to starve the city in earnest.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The siege of Cathair dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Ford and the Fouled Wells
told_in.section: VI. Of Cathair dhomhain, and the Wells

events.title: The wells of Cathair dhomhain foul
events.body: With no ground left beyond the walls to spare for burying, the dead of the siege lines are laid near the well-heads of Cathair dhomhain, and a sickness of the gut runs through the crowded streets and then through the garrison itself.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The siege of Cathair dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Ford and the Fouled Wells
told_in.section: VI. Of Cathair dhomhain, and the Wells

events.title: The garrison of Cathair dhomhain freed on oath
events.body: Catrìona nic Aonghais takes the surrender of Niall Mòr mac Leòid on the fortieth day of the siege and lets his garrison march out between her silent lines, wounded and dead named and carried, on his sworn word not to take the field against her again.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The siege of Cathair dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Ford and the Fouled Wells
told_in.section: VII. Of the Oath, and the Garrison Walking Out

events.title: The siege of Cathair dhomhain
events.body: Catrìona nic Aonghais besieges Cathair dhomhain, which had declared for Dùghall, and takes it after forty days, when its wells are fouled by the dead of the siege lines. She lets the garrison go free on their oath.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Catrìona's answer to the ford

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The water gate of Cathair dhomhain is closed

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The wells of Cathair dhomhain foul

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The garrison of Cathair dhomhain freed on oath

events.title: The hearths refused
events.body: Raghnall Ruadh, holding the vein-house, denies the measured handful of coal to every hearth and temple in the shires that stand against him. Hearths lit with the coal for generations go cold, and this deed turns more against him than any battle.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The store-master's list

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The temple fires of the cold shires go out

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The verse of the cold shires

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eòghann keeps Raghnall's list unscraped

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The store-master's board copied in full

events.title: The store-master's list
events.body: At Taigh na Fèithe Raghnall Ruadh hands the store-master Eòghann mac Dhùghaill a board naming every hearth and temple in the shires that stand against him and orders none of them measured a handful. The carriers who had come up the white road go down again with empty baskets.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The hearths refused

told_in.book: Of the Hearths Refused
told_in.section: III. Of the White Road

events.title: The temple fires of the cold shires go out
events.body: Without the measured handful, hearths and temple fires across the shires that stood for Catrìona or Dùghall go grey through Dubhlas, among them the Macha temple at Cathair mhòr where the burned households of Doire mhin have wintered on charity, Seònaid nic Coinnich's family among them.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hearths refused

told_in.book: Of the Hearths Refused
told_in.section: II. Of the Cold Shires

events.title: The verse of the cold shires
events.body: A verse with no name to it goes about the cold shires that winter, sung over mended hearths and unmended ones alike: that no battle was lost, only the fire. It is remembered afterward as the first telling that named what Raghnall's refusal had done.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hearths refused

told_in.book: Of the Hearths Refused
told_in.section: II. Of the Cold Shires

events.title: The pact of Catrìona and Dùghall
events.body: Dùghall Garbh comes to Catrìona nic Aonghais's camp with six men and no herald and offers to join their hosts against Raghnall Ruadh, saying that whichever of them wins the crown after this, it must not be a crown that can shut a door on a shire's hearths.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The battle of Muileann chrom

told_in.book: Of the Hearths Refused
told_in.section: III. Of the White Road

events.title: The battle of Muileann chrom
events.body: The hosts of Catrìona and Dùghall, joined for the purpose, meet Raghnall Ruadh below Muileann chrom. Raghnall falls on the field, and the next day his own custodians open the vein-house.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The pact of Catrìona and Dùghall

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Taigh na Fèithe opened

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first hearth relit

events.title: Taigh na Fèithe opened
events.body: The morning after Raghnall Ruadh falls at Muileann chrom, his own custodians strike the seal from the store without waiting to be told which claimant now holds the mountain, and the carriers go up the white road again.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The battle of Muileann chrom

told_in.book: Of the Hearths Refused
told_in.section: III. Of the White Road

events.title: The first hearth relit
events.body: Word reaches Catrìona at Taigh na Fèithe that the temple fire at Cathair mhòr, built up all winter from borrowed turf and hedge-wood, has caught at last on coal from a carrier's basket, the first of the cold shires' hearths to burn again.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The battle of Muileann chrom

told_in.book: Of the Hearths Refused
told_in.section: III. Of the White Road

events.title: Death of Dùghall Garbh
events.body: Dùghall Garbh dies at Baile Mòr dhomhain of the wounds he took at Muileann chrom. His followers go over to Catrìona without further fighting.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Dùghall Garbh dies of his wound

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dùghall's captains come over unbidden

events.title: Dùghall Garbh dies of his wound
events.body: Dùghall Garbh dies at Baile Mòr dhomhain of a cut taken below the arm at Muileann chrom that he hid from his own physicians for days. Catrìona nic Aonghais rides three days to reach him and finds him already dead, his last words asking only whether Taigh na Fèithe gates stood open.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Death of Dùghall Garbh

told_in.book: Of Catrìona Bhuadhach
told_in.section: I. Of the Wound That Would Not Close

events.title: Dùghall's captains come over unbidden
events.body: Dùghall Garbh's captains, led by Artair mac Lachlainn, come to Catrìona's camp within the fortnight and lay no terms before her, saying only that their dead lord had told them what he meant to do if the battle at Muileann chrom went their way, and that his word binds them still.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Dùghall Garbh

told_in.book: Of Catrìona Bhuadhach
told_in.section: I. Of the Wound That Would Not Close

events.title: Catrìona Bhuadhach crowned
events.body: Catrìona nic Aonghais is crowned at Cathair dhearg, and is known thereafter as Catrìona Bhuadhach. So ends the War of the Three Claimants, after some ten years.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Catrìona crowned at An Talla Dearg

events.title: Catrìona crowned at An Talla Dearg
events.body: Catrìona nic Aonghais is crowned at Cathair dhearg with little ceremony, the crown itself sent down under guard from Taigh na Fèithe's own custody. The seven heads swear to her in the old order, and she is called Catrìona Bhuadhach from that year.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Catrìona Bhuadhach crowned

told_in.book: Of Catrìona Bhuadhach
told_in.section: I. Of the Wound That Would Not Close

events.title: Eòghann keeps Raghnall's list unscraped
events.body: Eòghann mac Dhùghaill, still master of the store at Taigh na Fèithe, leaves Raghnall Ruadh's list of refused hearths standing face to the wall in the storeroom and sends word, unasked, that the store will not go a season again without measuring the handful while he holds the beam.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hearths refused

told_in.book: Of Catrìona Bhuadhach
told_in.section: I. Of the Wound That Would Not Close

events.title: The ruling of the hearth
events.body: Catrìona Bhuadhach and the vein-house set down in law that no claimant, house or king may withhold the measured handful from any lawful hearth. It is the first law written to bind the custodians themselves.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The drafting of Riaghailt an Teallaich

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The seven heads set their marks

events.title: The drafting of Riaghailt an Teallaich
events.body: At Taigh na Fèithe's own yard Catrìona and the seven heads of the houses spend three days drafting one sentence binding any claimant, house or king from ever again withholding the measured handful. Eòghann mac Dhùghaill is called to testify what Raghnall Ruadh said to him, and his flat account settles the argument the queen's own words could not.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The ruling of the hearth

told_in.book: Of Catrìona Bhuadhach
told_in.section: II. Of the Sentence in the Yard

events.title: The seven heads set their marks
events.body: Riaghailt an Teallaich is entered into Leabhar a' Chùraim beside Lagh an Loscaidh Bhig in the same hand, and the seven heads of the houses set their marks to it one after another, Beathag nic Uisdein of Clann Ìomhair last and longest over her own mark.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The ruling of the hearth

told_in.book: Of Catrìona Bhuadhach
told_in.section: II. Of the Sentence in the Yard

events.title: Birth of Lachlann mac Iain
events.body: A son, Lachlann, is born at Cathair dhearg to Queen Catrìona Bhuadhach, nine-and-thirty years old and three years crowned, and her husband Iain mac Eachainn.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Death of Lachlann mac Iain

told_in.book: Of Catrìona Bhuadhach
told_in.section: IV. Of the Single Day

events.title: Seònaid nic Coinnich comes to An Talla Dearg
events.body: Seònaid nic Coinnich, whose father Coinneach mac Ailein came through the winter of the refusal with a cough he never lost, walks up from Cathair mhòr to An Talla Dearg and is taken into the queen's household as a clerk, the first of several children of the cold shires the household shelters in those years.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Book of the Three Claimants

told_in.book: Of Catrìona Bhuadhach
told_in.section: III. Of the Clerk and the Road

events.title: Seònaid copies the tallies of the refusal
events.body: In her first winter at An Talla Dearg, Seònaid nic Coinnich asks to see Leabhar a' Chùraim's oldest entries and copies out, unbidden, the tallies of the hearths refused in the winter of Na Teallaichean Fuara, a labour the queen never questions when she comes upon it by lamplight.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Book of the Three Claimants

told_in.book: Of Catrìona Bhuadhach
told_in.section: III. Of the Clerk and the Road

events.title: The council questions Rathad na Banrighinn
events.body: More than one head of house asks Catrìona in open council why she spends so much of the treasury on a stone road to her own town of Inis thais. She answers that a kingdom bound by a law written in a cold yard ought to be bound also by roads a hard winter cannot cut, and the building goes on.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Catrìona's road south

told_in.book: Of Catrìona Bhuadhach
told_in.section: III. Of the Clerk and the Road

events.title: Catrìona's road south
events.body: Queen Catrìona has the road south from the capital by Baile shean and Am Buabhall Fortanach at Doire shean laid with stone, that her own town of Inis thais may be reached in any weather. It is called Rathad na Banrighinn.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The council questions Rathad na Banrighinn

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Rathad na Banrighinn laid to Inis thais

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first carters run Rathad na Banrighinn

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Death of Iain mac Eachainn

events.title: Rathad na Banrighinn laid to Inis thais
events.body: The stone of Rathad na Banrighinn is finished south from the capital, past Am Buabhall Fortanach at Doire shean, all the way to Catrìona's own gate at Inis thais, which she has ridden the length of twice while it was building to feel whether the stone held.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Catrìona's road south

told_in.book: Of Catrìona Bhuadhach
told_in.section: III. Of the Clerk and the Road

events.title: The first carters run Rathad na Banrighinn
events.body: Salt-carts and grain-carts run the full length of the new stone road within the year the last stone is laid, cutting the journey from three days to two. An old carter tells the household he drove it half-blind and felt the cart go steady the whole way, a thing the mire road never let him do.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Catrìona's road south

told_in.book: Of Catrìona Bhuadhach
told_in.section: III. Of the Clerk and the Road

events.title: Seann Warr's gates honoured
events.body: In memory of its standing aside in the war, Queen Catrìona grants Seann Warr the right to keep its own gates and take its own tolls. The grant is cut over the landward gate.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Seann Warr's grant cut over the gate

events.title: Death of Iain mac Eachainn
events.body: Iain mac Eachainn, the queen's husband, dies of a wasting in the chest no physician of the household can name. He had kept, through his years in An Talla Dearg, to the smaller business of the household and left the crown's affairs to Catrìona.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Catrìona's road south

told_in.book: Of Catrìona Bhuadhach
told_in.section: III. Of the Clerk and the Road

events.title: Seann Warr's grant cut over the gate
events.body: In memory of its standing aside through the war and the two sieges it withstood, Catrìona grants Seann Warr the right to keep its own gates and take its own tolls, and the grant is cut in stone letters over the landward gate.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Seann Warr's gates honoured

told_in.book: Of Catrìona Bhuadhach
told_in.section: III. Of the Clerk and the Road

events.title: Birth of Anna
events.body: A daughter, Anna, is born at Cathair dhearg to Lachlann mac Iain, the queen's son, then five-and-thirty; the old queen, seventy-four, lives to see her granddaughter walk.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Death of Lachlann mac Iain

told_in.book: Of Catrìona Bhuadhach
told_in.section: IV. Of the Single Day

events.title: Seònaid gathers the first three witnesses
events.body: At Queen Catrìona's own asking, her clerk Seònaid nic Coinnich takes down, in hurried hours snatched from the court's business, the first accounts of the war of the three claims: a soldier who fought at the ford, the son of Taigh na Fèithe's store-master, and a woman of Doire mhin who remembers Na Teallaichean Fuara as a child.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Book of the Three Claimants

told_in.book: Of the Book of the Three Claimants
told_in.section: II. Of the Witnesses

events.title: Death of Catrìona Bhuadhach
events.body: Catrìona Bhuadhach dies at Cathair dhearg. Her son Lachlann mac Iain is crowned, and the houses swear to him in a single day, a thing the chroniclers remark on.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Death of Catrìona Bhuadhach

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Na Seachd Taighean swear in a single day

events.title: Death of Catrìona Bhuadhach
events.body: Catrìona Bhuadhach dies at Cathair dhearg at seventy-eight, the last ruler to have fought in Cogadh nan Trì Tagraichean. Her son Lachlann mac Iain, not yet forty, succeeds her.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Death of Catrìona Bhuadhach

told_in.book: Of Catrìona Bhuadhach
told_in.section: IV. Of the Single Day

events.title: Na Seachd Taighean swear in a single day
events.body: The seven heads of the houses swear to Lachlann mac Iain within a single day of his mother's burial, Beathag nic Uisdein of Clann Ìomhair first to kneel. Seònaid nic Coinnich, watching from the back of the hall, counts the swearings without meaning to and goes that evening to begin the opening words of her history of the war.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Catrìona Bhuadhach

told_in.book: Of Catrìona Bhuadhach
told_in.section: IV. Of the Single Day

events.title: Seònaid visits the harbour-house boards
events.body: Carrying a grant of harbour dues she did not need to carry in her own hand, Seònaid nic Coinnich asks the harbour scribe Ailean mac Mhurchaidh to show her the old boards of Rolla nan Deònach, and rides home with an errand for herself she had not had when she set out.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Book of the Three Claimants

told_in.book: Of the Book of the Three Claimants
told_in.section: I. Of the Old Boards

events.title: The store-master's board copied in full
events.body: Dòmhnall mac Eòghainn, who inherited his father Eòghann mac Dhùghaill's office at Taigh na Fèithe's store, lets Seònaid nic Coinnich copy in full the board of shires refused the coal in the year of Na Teallaichean Fuara, a board his father kept face to the wall and never scraped clean.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hearths refused

told_in.book: Of the Book of the Three Claimants
told_in.section: II. Of the Witnesses

events.title: The witness of Doire mhin heard in full
events.body: Seònaid nic Coinnich rides to Cathair mhòr to hear Mairead nic Aonghais, a woman of Doire mhin who was a child in the same charity and at the same temple as Seònaid herself, tell at length what a cold hearth was to a child too young to be told why it was cold.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Book of the Three Claimants

told_in.book: Of the Book of the Three Claimants
told_in.section: II. Of the Witnesses

events.title: Seònaid weighs Leabhar a' Chùraim against her witnesses
events.body: At Taigh na Fèithe Seònaid nic Coinnich sets her gathered testimony against Leabhar a' Chùraim's own entries of the war, and finds days, numbers and causes of death the book and the witnesses do not agree on; she resolves to keep both accounts rather than choose between them.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Book of the Three Claimants

told_in.book: Of the Book of the Three Claimants
told_in.section: III. Of the Custody-Book at the Mountain

events.title: Fearchar Ciar swears the ford broke on two days
events.body: Where Leabhar a' Chùraim gives the breaking at the ford of Àth shean as one day, the old soldier Fearchar Ciar swears to Seònaid nic Coinnich that it was two, the fighting taken up again at first light after a night neither side thought worth entering.

links.label: Answers
links.title: The ford at Àth shean

told_in.book: Of the Book of the Three Claimants
told_in.section: II. Of the Witnesses

events.title: King Lachlann reads his mother into the book
events.body: Lachlann mac Iain finds Seònaid nic Coinnich at work on her history and asks whether it will say what his mother Catrìona was like; she answers that it will say what she did and what was believed of her, which is the most any book can give.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Book of the Three Claimants

told_in.book: Of the Book of the Three Claimants
told_in.section: I. Of the Old Boards

events.title: The Book of the Three Claimants
events.body: Seònaid nic Coinnich, once a clerk of Queen Catrìona's household, writes the story of the war from the custody-book and from the witness of those who fought. It is the oldest history of Dia-thìr that survives written as one tale and not as entries.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Seònaid nic Coinnich comes to An Talla Dearg

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Seònaid copies the tallies of the refusal

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Seònaid gathers the first three witnesses

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Seònaid visits the harbour-house boards

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The witness of Doire mhin heard in full

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Seònaid weighs Leabhar a' Chùraim against her witnesses

links.label: Caused by
links.title: King Lachlann reads his mother into the book

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Seònaid finishes Leabhar nan Trì Tagraichean

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Leabhar nan Trì Tagraichean read at An Talla Dearg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Death of Seònaid nic Coinnich

events.title: The sickness at Inis chrom
events.body: A spotted fever kills some forty at Inis chrom on the south-west coast. The Fianna of the Stone nurse the sick, and many of them die of it; thereafter the town is the Stone's.

events.title: Seònaid finishes Leabhar nan Trì Tagraichean
events.body: Seònaid nic Coinnich writes the last of the war's telling and sets down the finished leaves, the first history on Dia-thìr told as one tale from end to end rather than as separate entries.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The Book of the Three Claimants

told_in.book: Of the Book of the Three Claimants
told_in.section: V. Of the Reading at the Red Hall

events.title: Leabhar nan Trì Tagraichean read at An Talla Dearg
events.body: King Lachlann mac Iain has Seònaid nic Coinnich's finished history read into the record at An Talla Dearg and orders it copied again and kept, ruling that no later copy of it may ever be made shorter than the one before it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Book of the Three Claimants

told_in.book: Of the Book of the Three Claimants
told_in.section: V. Of the Reading at the Red Hall

events.title: Death of Seònaid nic Coinnich
events.body: Seònaid nic Coinnich dies at Cathair dhearg at two-and-eighty, seven years after finishing her book, her last recorded word a complaint that the harbour-house's back room at Seann Skell wants a better roof before the damp takes its oldest boards.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Book of the Three Claimants

told_in.book: Of the Book of the Three Claimants
told_in.section: V. Of the Reading at the Red Hall

events.title: The oyster beds of Doire shean
events.body: Doire shean, a village on the southern shore, lays out oyster beds in its shallow bay and sends oysters by cart to the capital. The trade makes it rich enough to be a shire seat.

events.title: Birth of the heir of Anna
events.body: A child is born at Cathair dhearg to Anna, Lachlann mac Iain's daughter, then five-and-thirty years old; Clàr nan Rìghrean keeps the year of the birth and lets the child's name fall from every copy that survives.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Death of Lachlann mac Iain

told_in.book: Of the Book of the Three Claimants
told_in.section: I. Of the Old Boards

events.title: The feast-market at Seann Tarr
events.body: The crowds that come to the ancestor shrine at Seann Tarr for the great feasts begin to hold a market on the three feast days, chiefly of honey, beeswax for the shrine lights, and the dyes of Baile fhiadhaich. The wax lights of Seann Tarr are soon burned at ancestor shrines all along the north-eastern coast.

events.title: Manannan preached at Seann Skell
events.body: At Seann Skell, where the sting-creed of the Holy Age first called itself the only true one, the preacher Mànas mac Ruairidh proclaims its one power to be Manannan mac Lir, lord of the sea, whose Cup of Truth bears the yellow scorpion. He teaches that Manannan shut the eastern sea behind the fleet with his mist, which hides Dia-thìr from every ship beyond it, and that the crossing must not be tried again. His hearers are the first congregation of Òrd Mhanannain, the order of Manannan.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ruairidh kneels first to Cupa na Fìrinne

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first boats blessed at Cidhe an Diosail

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The harbour-court's scribe refuses the order's rite

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Taigh Mhanannain raised at Seann Skell

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Death of Mànas mac Ruairidh

events.title: Death of Lachlann mac Iain
events.body: Lachlann mac Iain, son of Catrìona Bhuadhach, dies at Cathair dhearg, and his daughter Anna is crowned. The chroniclers call his reign quiet, and mean it as praise.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of Lachlann mac Iain

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of Anna

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Birth of the heir of Anna

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Tidings of the king's death reach the quay

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Death of Queen Anna

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The fourth ruler of the house of Catrìona crowned

events.title: Ruairidh kneels first to Cupa na Fìrinne
events.body: At Seann Skell, Ruairidh, a sworn-man of the harbour-court, crosses the quay stones and kneels before his own son Mànas mac Ruairidh, the first of the preaching's hearers to do so. Six other net-menders kneel after him before the tide has gone out much further.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Manannan preached at Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of Manannan's Cup
told_in.section: I. Of the Preaching on the Quay

events.title: Tidings of the king's death reach the quay
events.body: A rider watering his horse at Seann Skell's harbour-court brings word that Lachlann mac Iain has died at Cathair dhearg, eighty-nine years old after a reign of fifty quiet years, and that his daughter Anna, fifty-four, has been crowned in his place. Mànas mac Ruairidh is not recorded to have said anything of it.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Death of Lachlann mac Iain

told_in.book: Of Manannan's Cup
told_in.section: I. Of the Preaching on the Quay

events.title: The first boats blessed at Cidhe an Diosail
events.body: A dozen coasters are brought up one after another to Cidhe an Diosail at Seann Skell, and Mànas mac Ruairidh passes a plain wooden bowl of harbour water over each hull in turn, speaking the words that harden, within his own lifetime, into the fixed form of the rite of blessing.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Manannan preached at Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of Manannan's Cup
told_in.section: I. Of the Preaching on the Quay

events.title: The harbour-court's scribe refuses the order's rite
events.body: Donnchadh mac Ailein, scribe of the harbour-court at Seann Skell, refuses to enter the blessings of Òrd Mhanannain in Rolla a' Chalaidh beside the tallies of hulls and cargoes, holding a rite to be no business of a board kept for hulls. Mànas does not press the matter.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Manannan preached at Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of Manannan's Cup
told_in.section: I. Of the Preaching on the Quay

events.title: Manannan's order at Ros bheag and Cuan shean
events.body: Fishing families carry the teaching of Manannan's order down the west coast to Ros bheag and Cuan shean. At Cuan shean the rope-makers are among the first to turn to it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod Ciar swears Cupa na Fìrinne on the rope-walk

events.title: Tormod Ciar swears Cupa na Fìrinne on the rope-walk
events.body: At Cuan shean, the old rope-walker Tormod Ciar, told by a travelling net-mender what Mànas mac Ruairidh preaches of the mist, swears Cupa na Fìrinne before his fellow walkers on the rope-walk itself, cupping rainwater in his own hands for want of a bowl, with no priest of the order present to hear him.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Manannan's order at Ros bheag and Cuan shean

told_in.book: Of Manannan's Cup
told_in.section: II. Of the Cup Carried Down the Coast

events.title: Taigh Mhanannain raised at Seann Skell
events.body: Òrd Mhanannain raises its own house at Seann Skell, Taigh Mhanannain, low and built of the same grey stone as the quay near the old harbour-court. The congregation raises the silver for a proper cup without being asked, to replace the plain wooden bowl Mànas has used since the first blessing.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Manannan preached at Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of Manannan's Cup
told_in.section: I. Of the Preaching on the Quay

events.title: Birth of the fifth ruler of the house of Catrìona
events.body: A child is born at Cathair dhearg to Anna's heir, then five-and-forty years old, in the six-and-twentieth year of Queen Anna's reign; Clàr nan Rìghrean keeps the year and not the name.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Queen Eilidh Bhàn crowned

told_in.book: Of Manannan's Cup
told_in.section: I. Of the Preaching on the Quay

events.title: Death of Queen Anna
events.body: Queen Anna dies at Cathair dhearg at five-and-eighty, one-and-thirty years crowned, the last of the house of Catrìona whose name Clàr nan Rìghrean keeps for more than a century.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Lachlann mac Iain

told_in.book: Of Manannan's Cup
told_in.section: I. Of the Preaching on the Quay

events.title: The fourth ruler of the house of Catrìona crowned
events.body: Anna's heir is crowned at Cathair dhearg within the season, fifty years old. Clàr nan Rìghrean keeps the reign's years and not its name.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Lachlann mac Iain

told_in.book: Of Manannan's Cup
told_in.section: I. Of the Preaching on the Quay

events.title: Death of Mànas mac Ruairidh
events.body: Mànas mac Ruairidh dies at Seann Skell in the house he raised, six-and-thirty years after his first preaching on the quay, and is buried at his own asking under a plain slab facing the harbour mouth. Beathag nic Dhonnchaidh, who kept his house, keeps Taigh Mhanannain after him.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Manannan preached at Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of Manannan's Cup
told_in.section: II. Of the Cup Carried Down the Coast

events.title: Within sight of land
events.body: The priests of Manannan at Ros bheag lay down that no boat of the faithful may go out of sight of the headlands. The rule is kept on the west coast for centuries, and steering by the stars, already half lost, is lost there wholly.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The rule of the headlands laid down

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Coinneach mac Sheumais turned back within the year

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Griogair cannot name his grandfather's star

events.title: The rule of the headlands laid down
events.body: After a winter's debate, the priests of Òrd Mhanannain at Ros bheag lay down that no boat of the faithful may sail out of sight of the headlands, on pain of answering for it before Cupa na Fìrinne. The rule holds on the west coast far beyond any one preacher's lifetime.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Within sight of land

told_in.book: Of Manannan's Cup
told_in.section: III. Of the Rule of the Headlands

events.title: Coinneach mac Sheumais turned back within the year
events.body: Coinneach mac Sheumais, a skipper of Ros bheag, is turned back within the rule's first year by two of the order's own boats after taking his own boat further out than before, chasing a good run of fish. He never fishes so far out again.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Within sight of land

told_in.book: Of Manannan's Cup
told_in.section: III. Of the Rule of the Headlands

events.title: Griogair cannot name his grandfather's star
events.body: A priest of Òrd Mhanannain at Ros bheag asks a boy named Griogair, grandson of one of the last pilots to hold a course by night on that shore, which star his grandfather steered by. The boy cannot answer, and no one in his own house had thought to write the star's name down.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Within sight of land

told_in.book: Of Manannan's Cup
told_in.section: III. Of the Rule of the Headlands

events.title: The granaries of Àth shean rebuilt
events.body: The royal granaries at Àth shean, standing since before the Sundering, are pulled down and built again in stone on raised floors against the rats. The tally-house is rebuilt with them.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The granaries of Àth shean rebuilt

events.title: The granaries of Àth shean rebuilt
events.body: The royal granaries at Àth shean, standing since before a' Scaradh, are pulled down and rebuilt in dressed stone on raised floors against the rats, along with a new tally-house. Fearchar mac Phàdraig, the reeve who oversees the three-year labour, sees the shire's grain stand dry through its first winter.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The granaries of Àth shean rebuilt

told_in.book: Of Manannan's Cup
told_in.section: III. Of the Rule of the Headlands

events.title: Murchadh Beag takes Eòghann mac Pheadair from the coal-face
events.body: The old scribe of Taigh na Fèithe, Murchadh Beag, hears a coal-breaker's young son recite back a whole day's cartage without once looking at the board, and asks the boy's father whether a household might spare him for a scribe's stool. Eòghann mac Pheadair is set to sweep Taigh na Fèithe floor and mix ink before he is let touch a leaf.

told_in.book: Of the Bargain of the Counts
told_in.section: I. Of the Boy Set to the Tallies

events.title: The rope-walks shortened
events.body: Cuan shean takes up half its rope-walks and sows the ground with barley. The rope trade had lived on the fleet and then on the fishing, and the fishing no longer needs rope of such length.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Taigh na Fèithe's leaf takes in the rope-ground sown with barley

events.title: Taigh na Fèithe's leaf takes in the rope-ground sown with barley
events.body: Eòghann mac Pheadair, fourteen and newly trusted with a leaf of his own, enters the ground given up by Cuan shean's rope-walks for barley, the first entry he copies whose full sense Murchadh Beag has to explain to him. He learns that a scribe's business is the fact and the year, not the grief behind it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The rope-walks shortened

told_in.book: Of the Bargain of the Counts
told_in.section: I. Of the Boy Set to the Tallies

events.title: Death of the fourth ruler of the house of Catrìona
events.body: The fourth ruler of the house of Catrìona dies at Cathair dhearg at seven-and-eighty after seven-and-thirty years crowned, and the heir, two-and-forty years old, is crowned the same season.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Queen Eilidh Bhàn crowned

told_in.book: Of the Bargain of the Counts
told_in.section: V. Of the Year the World Went On Without Him

events.title: Wave at Cnoc chaol
events.body: A great swell with no storm behind it runs up the beach at Cnoc chaol on the south coast and carries off the drying racks and two children. The village sets its racks higher up the shore.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eòghann mac Pheadair at four-and-twenty

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A household of Cnoc chaol removes its gallery-claim from the shore

events.title: Eòghann mac Pheadair at four-and-twenty
events.body: At four-and-twenty Eòghann mac Pheadair has old Murchadh Beag's stool at Taigh na Fèithe as good as his own, and enters the wave at Cnoc chaol on the general leaf as he enters every disaster that touches a household of the coal-right: names, place, day.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Wave at Cnoc chaol

told_in.book: Of the Bargain of the Counts
told_in.section: II. Of the Wave and the Market

events.title: A household of Cnoc chaol removes its gallery-claim from the shore
events.body: After the great wave that took two children from the beach at Cnoc chaol, the household of one of the drowned strikes itself from its old gallery and takes up a new claim further from the water. Eòghann mac Pheadair enters the removal on Taigh na Fèithe's leaf the following season, cold and plain as he was taught.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Wave at Cnoc chaol

told_in.book: Of the Bargain of the Counts
told_in.section: II. Of the Wave and the Market

events.title: The market of the eastern road
events.body: Baile Mòr dhìreach, the citadel on the straight eastern road, is granted a market for the east coast. There the fish and sail-cloth of the coast towns meet the furs, hides and dyes of the hills, and the dyers of Baile Mòr ruadh sell their colours nowhere else.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eòghann mac Pheadair witnesses the market bounds at Baile Mòr dhìreach

events.title: Eòghann mac Pheadair witnesses the market bounds at Baile Mòr dhìreach
events.body: Sent east on his own feet for the first time, Eòghann mac Pheadair stands witness for Na Seachd Taighean when the crown's grant of a market is read at Baile Mòr dhìreach and its boundary stones set. He watches the first stalls go up the same afternoon and walks the road home slower than he walked out.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The market of the eastern road

told_in.book: Of the Bargain of the Counts
told_in.section: II. Of the Wave and the Market

events.title: Mòrag nic Ìomhair rides to Taigh na Fèithe with the crown's leaves
events.body: A scribe of An Talla Dearg's own household, Mòrag nic Ìomhair, rides the thirty-nine miles to Taigh na Fèithe at Muileann dhearg to set the crown's reckoning of Bliadhnaichean an Diosail against Leabhar a' Chùraim's own, after the two offices' counts are found not to agree. The master of Taigh na Fèithe grants her the book for as many days as the matter takes.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The two counts reconciled

told_in.book: Of the Bargain of the Counts
told_in.section: III. Of the Scribe of the Red Hall

events.title: The fault in the count is found and cannot be mended
events.body: Working three days by lamplight, Eòghann mac Pheadair and Mòrag nic Ìomhair trace the two offices' counts of An Diosal back to a single year, early after An Diosal, entered twice by one office's habit or once by the other's. Neither leaf either scribe has brought can say which office erred, or whether either truly has.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The two counts reconciled

told_in.book: Of the Bargain of the Counts
told_in.section: III. Of the Scribe of the Red Hall

events.title: The two counts reconciled
events.body: The vein-house and the crown's scribes find that their counts of years since the Setting-Out differ, and settle the difference by agreement. The same agreement fixes the day of the rite of the empty harbour, which each count had placed otherwise; later scribes cease to pretend it was fixed by proof.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Mòrag nic Ìomhair rides to Taigh na Fèithe with the crown's leaves

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The fault in the count is found and cannot be mended

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The two counts settled by agreement, not by proof

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The day of Deas-ghnàth a' Chalaidh Fhalaimh fixed

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The agreement-leaf folded into Leabhar a' Chùraim

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The coast keeps the rite on the agreed day

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: Eòghann mac Pheadair shows the agreement-leaf to his own pupil

events.title: The two counts settled by agreement, not by proof
events.body: Taigh na Fèithe and the crown's scribe take the crown's count for the reckoning that will go forward, since it touches more households than Taigh na Fèithe's own, and Eòghann mac Pheadair writes Taigh na Fèithe's agreement to it in his own hand. The master of Taigh na Fèithe's mark is set under his, and the crown scribe's office mark under that.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The two counts reconciled

told_in.book: Of the Bargain of the Counts
told_in.section: IV. Of the Agreement

events.title: The day of Deas-ghnàth a' Chalaidh Fhalaimh fixed
events.body: The same agreement that settles the count also fixes, for the first time, a single day on which Deas-ghnàth a' Chalaidh Fhalaimh is to be kept by every harbour of the coast together, in place of each keeping it a day or two either side of its neighbours by its own old custom. Mòrag nic Ìomhair carries word of it down to Seann Skell.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The two counts reconciled

told_in.book: Of the Bargain of the Counts
told_in.section: IV. Of the Agreement

events.title: The agreement-leaf folded into Leabhar a' Chùraim
events.body: Eòghann mac Pheadair keeps his copy of the sealed agreement between two older leaves of Leabhar a' Chùraim that had never before had a stranger's mark folded in among them. He tells the master of Taigh na Fèithe only that the crown's scribe was a hard woman to argue a figure past and an easy one to agree a figure with.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The two counts reconciled

told_in.book: Of the Bargain of the Counts
told_in.section: IV. Of the Agreement

events.title: The coast keeps the rite on the agreed day
events.body: Mòrag nic Ìomhair writes to Eòghann mac Pheadair the following winter that not a single harbour of the coast has written to complain of the day set for Deas-ghnàth a' Chalaidh Fhalaimh. Eòghann keeps the short note folded inside his own working leaves for the rest of his working life.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The two counts reconciled

told_in.book: Of the Bargain of the Counts
told_in.section: IV. Of the Agreement

events.title: Birth of Eilidh Bhàn
events.body: A girl, Eilidh, fair enough to be called Eilidh Bhàn from her first year, is born at Cathair dhearg, granddaughter of the ruler who has then held the hall nine-and-twenty years.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Queen Eilidh Bhàn crowned

told_in.book: Of the Bargain of the Counts
told_in.section: III. Of the Scribe of the Red Hall

events.title: Word of the disputation at Inis mhòr reaches Taigh na Fèithe
events.body: A rider carries north country talk to Taigh na Fèithe of a house of disputation newly founded at Inis mhòr, whose first master refuses every answer offered him on whether the vein answers any true count of years or only the custom of counting it. Eòghann mac Pheadair, old now, hears it out and goes back to his leaf.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The druid school at Inis mhòr

told_in.book: Of the Bargain of the Counts
told_in.section: V. Of the Year the World Went On Without Him

events.title: The druid school at Inis mhòr
events.body: Pupils of Dùn thais found a house of disputation at Inis mhòr, and the question of the vein is argued in the north for the first time. Its first master, Fionnlagh mac Aonghais, is remembered for refusing every answer offered him.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Word of the disputation at Inis mhòr reaches Taigh na Fèithe

events.title: Queen Eilidh Bhàn crowned
events.body: Eilidh Bhàn, sixth ruler of the house of Catrìona, is crowned at Cathair dhearg, a girl of eighteen. The annals of her long reign are almost wholly of harvests.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of the fifth ruler of the house of Catrìona

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Death of the fourth ruler of the house of Catrìona

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of Eilidh Bhàn

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The master of Taigh na Fèithe stands for Eòghann at the crowning

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Death of the fifth ruler of the house of Catrìona

events.title: The bath-house at the hot springs
events.body: Clann Choinnich rebuilds in dressed stone the old bath-house over the hot springs of Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh, and admits the sick of any house one day in seven. Its physicians keep a book of cures, afterwards lost.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Eòghann mac Pheadair is carried to the bath-house at Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh

events.title: The master of Taigh na Fèithe stands for Eòghann at the crowning
events.body: When Na Seachd Taighean' custodians go down to Cathair dhearg to see the new queen crowned, as the compact requires, the master of Taigh na Fèithe goes in place of Eòghann mac Pheadair, whose legs will no longer answer for a journey of thirty-nine miles in a single season. Eòghann hears the crowning described to him afterward by the returning master.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Queen Eilidh Bhàn crowned

told_in.book: Of the Bargain of the Counts
told_in.section: V. Of the Year the World Went On Without Him

events.title: Eòghann mac Pheadair is carried to the bath-house at Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh
events.body: In the last cold turn of the year, his chest gone tight in a way no winter before has managed, Eòghann mac Pheadair lets himself be carried by cart to the rebuilt bath-house below Muileann ruadh, where he sits in the warm water among coal-breakers, salt-carriers and a shepherd's widow, none of them minding whose gallery the others answer to.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The bath-house at the hot springs

told_in.book: Of the Bargain of the Counts
told_in.section: V. Of the Year the World Went On Without Him

events.title: Eòghann mac Pheadair shows the agreement-leaf to his own pupil
events.body: Asked by the young scribe he has lately taken to teaching what the finest thing was that he ever did in a life spent mostly at a stool, Eòghann mac Pheadair unfolds the thirty-year-old agreement-leaf and tells the boy it was not the count that made it worth keeping, but the honest agreement written under it.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The two counts reconciled

told_in.book: Of the Bargain of the Counts
told_in.section: V. Of the Year the World Went On Without Him

events.title: Death of the fifth ruler of the house of Catrìona
events.body: The fifth ruler of the house of Catrìona dies at Cathair dhearg at nine-and-eighty after seven-and-forty years crowned, and the crown passes to a granddaughter, Eilidh Bhàn, eighteen years old.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Queen Eilidh Bhàn crowned

told_in.book: Of the Bargain of the Counts
told_in.section: V. Of the Year the World Went On Without Him

events.title: A coaster boarded off the small islands
events.body: A coaster out of Ros bheag puts in at Baile chrom two days late and a third short in her hold, her skipper telling Coinneach mac Nèill, the reeve, that three boats out of the small islands boarded her and took her grain, wearing no mark and hiding no face.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The sea-thieves of the north-west

told_in.book: Of the Sea-Thieves' Strand
told_in.section: I. Of the Boats Off the Small Islands

events.title: The sea-thieves of the north-west
events.body: Boats out of the small islands off the north-west coast begin to rob the coasting traders of fish and grain. The sea-thieves are Dia-thìrich, men of the north-west shore, and the harbour rolls name some of them.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A coaster boarded off the small islands

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Rolla a' Chalaidh name Aonghas mac Ruairidh among the sea-thieves
