events.title: Rolla a' Chalaidh name Aonghas mac Ruairidh among the sea-thieves
events.body: The first full count of the takings sent up to Cathair dhearg names, among the sea-thieves of the small islands, a fisherman's son of Baile chrom, Aonghas mac Ruairidh. His mother tells the reeve plainly that a young man who watches the fish thin will go looking for a living wherever it is still to be found.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The sea-thieves of the north-west

told_in.book: Of the Sea-Thieves' Strand
told_in.section: I. Of the Boats Off the Small Islands

events.title: Baile chrom half empty
events.body: The reeve of Baile chrom on the north-west coast reports half the houses of the town empty, their families gone east before the sea-thieves and the poor harvests. The crown remits the town's grain dues.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Half of Baile chrom stands empty

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile chrom's grain dues remitted

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The reeve's letter asking for a force

events.title: Half of Baile chrom stands empty
events.body: Coinneach mac Nèill reports to the crown's scribes that half the houses of Baile chrom stand empty, their families gone inland before the sea-thieves and the failing catch, their thatch going to moss and their doors shut on rooms no one will sleep in again that year.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Baile chrom half empty

told_in.book: Of the Sea-Thieves' Strand
told_in.section: II. Of Half the Houses Standing Empty

events.title: Baile chrom's grain dues remitted
events.body: The crown remits Baile chrom's grain dues to a sum reckoned by the households that stand rather than the households that once stood, answering Coinneach mac Nèill's plain report with a plain word of thanks for a count taken with care.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Baile chrom half empty

told_in.book: Of the Sea-Thieves' Strand
told_in.section: II. Of Half the Houses Standing Empty

events.title: Birth of Dòmhnall Ruadh
events.body: A son, red-haired and called Dòmhnall Ruadh, is born at Muileann chrom to a custodian household of Clann Raghnaill that keeps three galleries under the mountain and has never once been asked into An Talla Dearg except to petition.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Dòmhnall Ruadh crowned

told_in.book: Of the Sea-Thieves' Strand
told_in.section: III. Of the Force Asked and the Force Sent

events.title: The reeve's letter asking for a force
events.body: After the sea-thieves put in twice within a single moon on strands within sight of his own harbour, Coinneach mac Nèill writes to the crown asking not for lightened dues this time but for an armed force, since a reeve with a tally-stick can no longer hold a coast his own shire's desperate sons have made their hunting ground.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Baile chrom half empty

told_in.book: Of the Sea-Thieves' Strand
told_in.section: III. Of the Force Asked and the Force Sent

events.title: Iain mac Thormoid raised against the small islands
events.body: Eilidh Bhàn raises a force under a captain named Iain mac Thormoid and sends it north by sea to Baile chrom, answering the reeve's long-waited letter. The captain charts the raiders' ground on Coinneach mac Nèill's own table with the help of the town's fishermen before the boats sail against the small islands.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The raid on Eilean dhubh

told_in.book: Of the Sea-Thieves' Strand
told_in.section: III. Of the Force Asked and the Force Sent

events.title: The raid on Eilean dhubh
events.body: A force sent by Queen Eilidh Bhàn lands on Eilean dhubh and burns the sea-thieves' boats on the strand. Their leader, Uilleam Ruadh, is taken to Cathair dhearg and hanged.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Iain mac Thormoid raised against the small islands

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Creach Eilean dhubh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Aonghas mac Ruairidh dies on the strand

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Uilleam Ruadh taken and hanged

events.title: Creach Eilean dhubh
events.body: Iain mac Thormoid's boats land at first light on Eilean dhubh and burn the sea-thieves' hulls on the strand, Coinneach mac Nèill's own fishermen leading the way through the channel among the small islands. The sea-thieves, unwatched for the better part of a decade, are taken all but by surprise.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The raid on Eilean dhubh

told_in.book: Of the Sea-Thieves' Strand
told_in.section: III. Of the Force Asked and the Force Sent

events.title: Aonghas mac Ruairidh dies on the strand
events.body: Aonghas mac Ruairidh, thirty-one years old and once a boy Coinneach mac Nèill carried on his own shoulder to this same water, is killed defending a hull on Eilean dhubh's strand. The reeve kneels over him and finds he has no words ready for the mother he must tell of it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The raid on Eilean dhubh

told_in.book: Of the Sea-Thieves' Strand
told_in.section: III. Of the Force Asked and the Force Sent

events.title: Uilleam Ruadh taken and hanged
events.body: Uilleam Ruadh, leader of the sea-thieves for the better part of a decade, is taken alive off Eilean dhubh's strand and carried south in irons to Cathair dhearg, where he is hanged before the season turns, six and thirty years old.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The raid on Eilean dhubh

told_in.book: Of the Sea-Thieves' Strand
told_in.section: III. Of the Force Asked and the Force Sent

events.title: The dearth on the north-west shore
events.body: A run of failed harvests along the north-west shore grows more than the shared-meal custom can carry. Coinneach mac Nèill keeps the custom at his own board as long as grain remains to keep it with, dividing what the diminished fields bring in as evenly as his hand can manage.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The dearth on the north-west shore

told_in.book: Of the Sea-Thieves' Strand
told_in.section: IV. Of the Harvests That Would Not Come

events.title: The dearth on the north-west shore
events.body: Harvest after harvest fails along the north-west shore, and the dearth is more than the shared meal can bear. Families leave the coast for the inland shires and the east, and the north-west is thinly held from this time to the end of the age.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The dearth on the north-west shore

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag nic Artair dies of the winter's sickness

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: Coinneach mac Nèill leaves Baile chrom

events.title: Beathag nic Artair dies of the winter's sickness
events.body: In the hard winter of the dearth, Beathag nic Artair, wife of the reeve of Baile chrom, dies of a chest complaint her body, weakened by two thin harvests running, has no strength left to fight. The last of the town's households load their carts and go inland and east the same season.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The dearth on the north-west shore

told_in.book: Of the Sea-Thieves' Strand
told_in.section: IV. Of the Harvests That Would Not Come

events.title: Coinneach mac Nèill leaves Baile chrom
events.body: Coinneach mac Nèill, reeve of Baile chrom for eight-and-forty years, sets the reeve's chest of rolls and tallies in order for a successor he no longer believes will come, shuts his own door behind him, and sets the coast road east under his feet.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The dearth on the north-west shore

told_in.book: Of the Sea-Thieves' Strand
told_in.section: V. Of the Roll Recopied and the Market at the Ford

events.title: Birth of Raghnall Òg
events.body: A son, Raghnall, is born at Muileann chrom to Dòmhnall Ruadh, then five-and-thirty years old and keeper of his house's three galleries.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Death of Dòmhnall Ruadh

told_in.book: Of the Sea-Thieves' Strand
told_in.section: I. Of the Boats Off the Small Islands

events.title: The king-list recopied
events.body: The scribes of Queen Eilidh Bhàn copy the king-list of Dia-thìr afresh from its oldest surviving roll, adding the rulers since the Sundering. The new copy begins the present age with the Choosing and not with the fleet.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Clàr nan Rìghrean recopied

events.title: Clàr nan Rìghrean recopied
events.body: The queen's scribes at Cathair dhearg take down the old Clàr nan Rìghrean from its resting place and copy it afresh onto new hide, adding every ruler since the fleet had gone and setting the new copy's beginning at An Roghnachadh rather than at the sailing.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The king-list recopied

told_in.book: Of the Sea-Thieves' Strand
told_in.section: V. Of the Roll Recopied and the Market at the Ford

events.title: The strand-market at Àth fhionn
events.body: A market grows up on the strand at Àth fhionn, where the coast road crosses the clear river, trading north-coast fish, the flesh and oil of stranded whales, wool and barley. The fishers of the north coast no longer carry their catch the longer road south to Inis mhòr.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The strand-market at Àth fhionn

told_in.book: Of the Sea-Thieves' Strand
told_in.section: V. Of the Roll Recopied and the Market at the Ford

events.title: The strand-market at Àth fhionn
events.body: Àth fhionn, the ford town where the coast road crosses the clear river, holds a market on the strand for the north coast, of fish, the flesh and oil of stranded whales, wool and barley. The fishers of the north coast no longer carry their catch to Inis mhòr.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The strand-market at Àth fhionn

events.title: Eilidh Bhàn dies without an heir
events.body: Queen Eilidh Bhàn dies at Cathair dhearg without a child, and the house of Catrìona ends with her. The seven houses meet at the vein-house and not at the capital.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Na Seachd Taighean ride to Taigh na Fèithe rather than An Talla Dearg

events.title: Na Seachd Taighean ride to Taigh na Fèithe rather than An Talla Dearg
events.body: On the queen's death Na Seachd Taighean' messengers pass over the empty capital and ride straight to Taigh na Fèithe above the mountain, choosing to settle the succession among the galleries and Clachan a' Chrannchuir rather than under the house of Catrìona's own roof. No leaf gives the reason; a young scribe of Taigh na Fèithe later says it felt from the first hour less like a choosing than a homecoming.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Eilidh Bhàn dies without an heir

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: I. Of the Empty Hall

events.title: Nine days at the long table
events.body: The heads of Na Seachd Taighean sit first nine days at the table under Taigh na Fèithe's north window, and ride up again at every season's turning for five years, while the capital's clerks hold grain prices and boundary pleas unanswered for want of anyone with standing to settle them. At the last sitting the name of Dòmhnall Ruadh of Muileann chrom is spoken and not spoken down again.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dòmhnall Ruadh crowned

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: I. Of the Empty Hall

events.title: Dòmhnall Ruadh crowned
events.body: The houses name Dòmhnall Ruadh of Clann Raghnaill, of the line of the claimant slain at Muileann chrom. He is crowned at Cathair dhearg and keeps the mastery of the vein-house with the crown.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of Dòmhnall Ruadh

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Nine days at the long table

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dòmhnall Ruadh told whose yard he stands in

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dòmhnall Ruadh's household summoned from Muileann chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dòmhnall Ruadh crowned at six-and-fifty

events.title: Dòmhnall Ruadh told whose yard he stands in
events.body: An old custodian takes the newly named Dòmhnall Ruadh aside in Taigh na Fèithe yard and tells him it is the same ground on which Raghnall Ruadh, of his own house, once refused every claimant offered him and shut the door on a season of refused hearths. Dòmhnall Ruadh says only that he hopes to prove a different answer to the same question.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dòmhnall Ruadh crowned

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: II. Of the Yard

events.title: Dòmhnall Ruadh's household summoned from Muileann chrom
events.body: Riders carry word to Muileann chrom for Dòmhnall Ruadh's wife and two grown sons to come up to Cathair dhearg; he spends his first night as king naming aloud which of his neighbours he trusts to keep his own galleries honestly measured in his absence, troubled more by that than by the crown awaiting him.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dòmhnall Ruadh crowned

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: II. Of the Yard

events.title: Dòmhnall Ruadh crowned at six-and-fifty
events.body: Dòmhnall Ruadh is crowned at Cathair dhearg nine days after the houses name him, six-and-fifty years old, in a hall his house had never in nearly three hundred years entered as anything but petitioner.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dòmhnall Ruadh crowned

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: II. Of the Yard

events.title: The king's horse known on the mountain road
events.body: Riding the thirty-nine miles between Cathair dhearg and Taigh na Fèithe so often in the first years of his reign, Dòmhnall Ruadh is known by his horse before his face, and the road's keepers complain that they never shod one animal so often in one man's service.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The crown and the custody joined

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: III. Of the Joining

events.title: The boundary stone of the shifted stream
events.body: Dòmhnall Ruadh rides down from the capital to Muileann chrom himself to settle a boundary dispute between two households of his own old neighbours, and fixes the stone's place by asking each household's oldest member, separately, where they remember playing as children, rather than by any measuring Taigh na Fèithe owns.

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: IV. Of the Mountain's Own King

events.title: The king keeps his seat at An Talla Dearg
events.body: Pressed by more than one of the seven heads to move the crown's seat to the mountain, since a king who is master of Taigh na Fèithe belongs among the galleries, Dòmhnall Ruadh keeps it at Cathair dhearg for the whole of his five-and-twenty years.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The crown and the custody joined

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: IV. Of the Mountain's Own King

events.title: The crown and the custody joined
events.body: Dòmhnall Ruadh's reeves write into the custody-book that the ruler of Dia-thìr is also master of the vein-house. Thereafter the heads of the seven houses sit as the king's council, and the custodians and the court are one body.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The king's horse known on the mountain road

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The king keeps his seat at An Talla Dearg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The reeve's entry read out to the king

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Leabhar a' Chùraim and the crown's rolls copied onto one shelf

events.title: The reeve's entry read out to the king
events.body: Dòmhnall Ruadh's reeve reads him the fair copy of the entry joining the crown to the mastery of Taigh na Fèithe before it is set to the king's own mark; Dòmhnall Ruadh says it reads less like a new law than a plain account of what has already been true since the morning in the yard, and the reeve agrees.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The crown and the custody joined

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: III. Of the Joining

events.title: Leabhar a' Chùraim and the crown's rolls copied onto one shelf
events.body: Taigh na Fèithe's clerks spend the better part of two years copying Leabhar a' Chùraim and the crown's rolls, kept apart under separate roofs for near three hundred years, onto the same shelves in the same hands, until no leaf of either record can be told from the other at a glance.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The crown and the custody joined

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: III. Of the Joining

events.title: The metalworker who cuts the seal
events.body: A metalworker of Muileann dhearg who has never before been asked to cut more than a gallery-marker spends near a season on the new seal's die, complaining that the gold will not sit against the blue as he wishes. Dòmhnall Ruadh, seeing it finished, says he can find nothing in it that is properly his to add.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The custody's seal on the king's letters

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: III. Of the Joining

events.title: The custody's seal on the king's letters
events.body: From the joining of the crown and the custody the king's letters bear the vein-house's own seal: a trellis of gold on blue, which the custodians read as the galleries of the mountain, and over it a hollow lozenge for Crom's slab, laid on the first break. The crown adds a white band across the field and nothing more. From this time the seal is the arms of the kingdom.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The metalworker who cuts the seal

events.title: Death of Dòmhnall Ruadh
events.body: Dòmhnall Ruadh, the first to hold both the crown and the vein-house, dies at Cathair dhearg and is buried at Muileann dhearg. His son Raghnall Òg is crowned.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of Raghnall Òg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dòmhnall Ruadh buried under the mountain

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall Òg asks to shorten his own coronation

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall Òg crowned at six-and-forty

events.title: Dòmhnall Ruadh buried under the mountain
events.body: Dòmhnall Ruadh is carried, by his own long-standing wish, not to the house of Catrìona's tombs at Cathair dhearg but up to Taigh na Fèithe, where the custodians dig his grave themselves in a worked-out gallery and lay him with a single unlit lamp at his head, a rite kept for no other ruler before or since.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Dòmhnall Ruadh

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: IV. Of the Mountain's Own King

events.title: Raghnall Òg asks to shorten his own coronation
events.body: At the rehearsal of his coronation Raghnall Òg twice asks the clerks whether the ceremony might be shortened by an hour so that he can see a shire plea before dark, more at ease already with a boundary dispute than with a court's ceremony.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Dòmhnall Ruadh

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: IV. Of the Mountain's Own King

events.title: Raghnall Òg crowned at six-and-forty
events.body: Raghnall Òg is crowned at Cathair dhearg after his father's burial under the mountain, six-and-forty years old, keeper already of the crown's shire pleas.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Dòmhnall Ruadh

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: IV. Of the Mountain's Own King

events.title: The schism of the Hawk
events.body: A council of the Hawk at Cnoc bheag divides over whether Mòd's measure may ever be raised. Those who hold it fixed for ever keep the name of the Hungry Hawk and the house at Cnoc bheag; those who hold that a greater flock may be fed a greater handful are called the Fed Hawk.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The young priest's question at Cnoc bheag

events.title: The young priest's question at Cnoc bheag
events.body: At the council of Òrd an t-Seabhaig a young priest rises to ask the elders whether Mòd himself would rather starve a grown flock than see his old handful grown to meet it. The council turns on the question, and An Seabhag Biadhte is named from that day.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The schism of the Hawk

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: V. Of the Hawk that Split

events.title: The harbour of Seann Chwen
events.body: Seann Chwen builds its harbour mole and becomes the port of the coal-carts coming down from the mountain to the coast towns of the south.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first barges tie up at Seann Chwen's new mole

events.title: The first barges tie up at Seann Chwen's new mole
events.body: The first coal-barges of the mountain roads tie up at Seann Chwen's finished stone mole where before they only beached on shingle at low water; a rider carrying the news south remarks that he rode the whole way under one seal without troubling to wonder which office he rode for.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The harbour of Seann Chwen

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: IV. Of the Mountain's Own King

events.title: The Fed Hawk at Seann Skell
events.body: The priests of the Fed Hawk, driven from Cnoc bheag, settle at Seann Skell on the north coast, not the western river port of that name. The custody-book writes their teaching down as an error, and at length.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag nic Sheumais builds An Seabhag Biadhte's house

events.title: Beathag nic Sheumais builds An Seabhag Biadhte's house
events.body: Beathag nic Sheumais, nineteen at the schism, builds An Seabhag Biadhte's following at Seann Skell on the north coast from four families to a proper school over two decades, within sound of a sea that has never given the island a word of what lies beyond it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Fed Hawk at Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: V. Of the Hawk that Split

events.title: The Fed Hawk's petition
events.body: From Seann Skell the Fed Hawk asks the king's council to raise the measured handful by a quarter for the hearths of the north coast. The council refuses. It is the first plea on record to alter the Small-Burning Law.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag nic Sheumais rides south to petition in person

events.title: Beathag nic Sheumais rides south to petition in person
events.body: Rather than trust the asking to a letter, Beathag nic Sheumais rides to Cathair dhearg herself in her fiftieth year and lays the north coast's cold winters before the seven heads without once raising her voice; the council refuses her at length, and she carries the refusal home in her own satchel.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Fed Hawk's petition

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: V. Of the Hawk that Split

events.title: The gallery at Cill ghlas
events.body: A second tremor in the hills of Cill ghlas brings down a gallery of the vein and kills fourteen labourers of the custodians. The vein-house closes the gallery and sets at its mouth a stone with the fourteen names.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The fourteen named at the gallery's mouth

events.title: The fourteen named at the gallery's mouth
events.body: Taigh na Fèithe sets a stone with the fourteen names of Cill ghlas cut in the order they went down, the youngest a boy of thirteen, the oldest a woman forty years at the same gallery. Households of the mountain take up the custom of leaving their own small stones at its foot on the day of the fall.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The gallery at Cill ghlas

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: VI. Of the Fourteen Names and the Posts on the Road

events.title: A head of the seven names the fourteen before the council
events.body: Laying the matter of the coal-roads before the king's council, one of the seven heads says plainly that fourteen names on a stone at a gallery's mouth are proof enough the mountain's coal is given up at a real cost, and that no house's quarrel has business stopping it on the road. None of the seven speaks against him.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The coal-roads kept by the crown

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: VI. Of the Fourteen Names and the Posts on the Road

events.title: The coal-roads kept by the crown
events.body: The king's council takes the roads from the mountain to the coast into the crown's keeping, that no house may stop the carts bearing the measured coal to the temples. The roads are marked with posts bearing the crown's sign: the carriers' road down to Cathair dhearg, An Rathad Tuath over the pass by Muileann fhada, Slighe Muileann dhearg south from the hills by Muileann chrom, and Slighe Baile òg down to the southern Seann Skell.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A head of the seven names the fourteen before the council

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The posts driven along the coal-roads

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A carter's answer, remembered afterward

events.title: The posts driven along the coal-roads
events.body: Coal-carters hired for the season and paid from the roads' own tolls drive posts the length of all four coal-roads through a single autumn, a trellis and a hollow stone cut at every shire joint, without ceremony or a word said over the last post.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The coal-roads kept by the crown

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: VI. Of the Fourteen Names and the Posts on the Road

events.title: A carter's answer, remembered afterward
events.body: A carter who helped set posts on three of the four coal-roads is asked the next spring what the work was like, and says only that a man can now walk any of them from the mountain to the sea and never lose the road for want of knowing whose it is; his answer outlives the council's own leaf of the debate.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The coal-roads kept by the crown

told_in.book: Of the Crown Joined to the Vein
told_in.section: VI. Of the Fourteen Names and the Posts on the Road

events.title: The crown's riders
events.body: Fresh horses are kept for the crown's riders at the waypoint houses on the coal-roads, and a rider changing at every house carries the council's word from Cathair dhearg to the mountain between dawn and dark. The stabling is paid out of the coal-road tolls.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mairead nic Aonghais's three tallies

events.title: Mairead nic Aonghais's three tallies
events.body: The keeper of a road-house on the northern coal-road keeps three notched sticks beside the reeve's own tally of the crown's riders: one for every rider through, one for those who thank her by name, and one for those carrying business she judges not worth the horse it rode on.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The crown's riders

told_in.book: Of the Stair under the Hill
told_in.section: I. Of the Road and the Empty Pastures

events.title: The high pastures of Doire uaine forsaken
events.body: The last shepherd families leave the high pastures of the Doire uaine hills for the valley villages. They give the grazing as the reason; every one of them speaks also of the Marbh-bheò.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The last shieling of Doire uaine

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A drover crosses the empty pastures

events.title: The last shieling of Doire uaine
events.body: An old woman drives her last three goats and a lame ewe down from her own shieling in the high pastures of Doire uaine, the last of her country to come down, and tells the priest who meets her at the valley's edge that a place can grow tired of being lived in alone by living things.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The high pastures of Doire uaine forsaken

told_in.book: Of the Stair under the Hill
told_in.section: I. Of the Road and the Empty Pastures

events.title: A drover crosses the empty pastures
events.body: A drover taking cattle to the lowland market by the old high road finds the whole stretch of the forsaken shielings of Doire uaine silent from end to end, not a dog barking nor a hearth smoking, and pushes his herd on rather than camp the night on ground nobody is left to grant or refuse.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The high pastures of Doire uaine forsaken

told_in.book: Of the Stair under the Hill
told_in.section: I. Of the Road and the Empty Pastures

events.title: The salt fair at Ros fhionn
events.body: Ros fhionn holds its great salt fair, and the reeve counts some four thousand people on the flats in a single day. It is the height of the town, and the chronicle calls it the richest place in the north-east.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Four thousand counted on the salt flats

events.title: Four thousand counted on the salt flats
events.body: The reeve of Ros fhionn's salt fair loses his own count somewhere past four thousand among the carts, pack-mules and children on the flats, and writes the figure down rounded rather than pretend to a precision the crowd never held still for.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The salt fair at Ros fhionn

told_in.book: Of the Stair under the Hill
told_in.section: I. Of the Road and the Empty Pastures

events.title: Cathair mhòr the largest town
events.body: Cathair mhòr, its market drawing the trade of all the south, grows greater than the capital. The capital remains the seat of the crown, and the lesser town.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A carter's plain answer

events.title: A carter's plain answer
events.body: Asked by a clerk of An Talla Dearg why he sells his barley at Cathair mhòr and not the capital, a carter of the southern road answers that a man carries his load to whichever gate opens first and pays best; the clerk enters the answer as given.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cathair mhòr the largest town

told_in.book: Of the Stair under the Hill
told_in.section: I. Of the Road and the Empty Pastures

events.title: The stair at Toll-dubh
events.body: Quarrymen north of the capital break into Toll-dubh, the shaft of the old tales, long lost, and find a stair cut in the rock going down beyond their lamps. The custodians of the vein-house wall up the entrance. The one quarryman who went down never tells what he saw.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The quarry face opens on Toll-dubh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Calum Dubh climbs the stair

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Leabhar a' Chùraim takes Calum Dubh's silence as given

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: A saying born of a silent man

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: Death of Calum Dubh mac Iain, still silent

events.title: The quarry face opens on Toll-dubh
events.body: A stubborn seam on the quarry face north of the capital swings inward on nothing and opens on a cold, scentless dark; the quarryman Calum Dubh mac Iain names the shaft Toll-dubh before any other man on the ledge can, and the whole crew falls silent.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The stair at Toll-dubh

told_in.book: Of the Stair under the Hill
told_in.section: II. Of the Stair under the Hill

events.title: Calum Dubh climbs the stair
events.body: Calum Dubh mac Iain goes down the stair of Toll-dubh alone with a lamp and a paid-out rope while his fellows watch the light dwindle and vanish; he climbs out again, sits a long while on the loose stone, and tells the foreman only that the face must be closed.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The stair at Toll-dubh

told_in.book: Of the Stair under the Hill
told_in.section: II. Of the Stair under the Hill

events.title: Leabhar a' Chùraim takes Calum Dubh's silence as given
events.body: Taigh na Fèithe's custodians wall the mouth of Toll-dubh within a month and enter Calum Dubh mac Iain's own brief account of the walling exactly as he gives it, adding nothing to fill out what he leaves unsaid.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The stair at Toll-dubh

told_in.book: Of the Stair under the Hill
told_in.section: II. Of the Stair under the Hill

events.title: The copper-workers of Cathair mhòr
events.body: The copper-workers of Cathair mhòr begin to make cooking pots, which are sold on every road of the island. Each bears its maker's sign, and some are still found in the ground.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The copper-workers' maker's marks

events.title: The copper-workers' maker's marks
events.body: The copper-workers of Cathair mhòr stamp every cooking pot with its own maker's mark, a leaf, a fish or a plain letter, and the pots go out on every road at once, carried by hands their makers will never meet.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The copper-workers of Cathair mhòr

told_in.book: Of the Stair under the Hill
told_in.section: III. Of the Ruins Ailean Measured

events.title: A saying born of a silent man
events.body: The quarry town takes up a way of speaking of any close-mouthed man, that he has gone down and come up like Calum Dubh, and the saying outgrows him within a generation, applied to men who never went near Toll-dubh at all.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The stair at Toll-dubh

told_in.book: Of the Stair under the Hill
told_in.section: II. Of the Stair under the Hill

events.title: Ailean measures Làrach an Teampaill
events.body: Ailean mac Dhùghaill, a scholar of the druid school at Dùn thais, measures the ruin of Làrach an Teampaill and writes that its altar faces the central mountains and not the sea. Who set it so he will not guess.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailean measures the temple-ruin's altar

events.title: Ailean measures the temple-ruin's altar
events.body: Ailean mac Dhùghaill lays his cord across the altar-stone of Làrach an Teampaill and finds it faces the central mountains, its back to the sea, a plain fact no teller of the ruin's tales had ever thought worth the mentioning; he says only that he will not guess who set the stone so.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ailean measures Làrach an Teampaill

told_in.book: Of the Stair under the Hill
told_in.section: III. Of the Ruins Ailean Measured

events.title: Birth of Mòrag Ruadh
events.body: A daughter, Mòrag, red-haired and called Mòrag Ruadh, is born into Clann Raghnaill; Leabhar a' Chùraim gives the house and the year, for no one yet has cause to write more.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Queen Mòrag Ruadh crowned

told_in.book: Of the Stair under the Hill
told_in.section: I. Of the Road and the Empty Pastures

events.title: The farmer's barrowload of stone
events.body: A farmer whose plough turns up stone every spring at the edge of his field meets Ailean mac Dhùghaill at Làrach an Dùin with a barrowload of it, half in earnest asking whether the school will pay for what his own ground keeps giving back; Ailean measures every stone and buys none of them.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailean's tables of the old ruins

told_in.book: Of the Stair under the Hill
told_in.section: III. Of the Ruins Ailean Measured

events.title: Ailean's tables of the old ruins
events.body: Ailean mac Dhùghaill finishes his tables of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire, Làrach an Dùin and Làrach an Teampaill, with the measure, stone and lie of each. He cannot say whether one people built all three, and because of his tables no scholar after him could say either.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The farmer's barrowload of stone

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The school judges Ailean's tables

events.title: The school judges Ailean's tables
events.body: The school at Dùn thais argues a winter over Ailean mac Dhùghaill's finished tables of the three old ruins and judges only that his measurements stand sound and his caution on their makers sounder still, closing the question no scholar after him could reopen.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ailean's tables of the old ruins

told_in.book: Of the Stair under the Hill
told_in.section: III. Of the Ruins Ailean Measured

events.title: Death of Calum Dubh mac Iain, still silent
events.body: Calum Dubh mac Iain dies in his own house in his sixty-fifth year, well liked in the quarry town for a quiet kindness, having told no living soul, wife, son or scribe, what he saw on the stair under the hill.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The stair at Toll-dubh

told_in.book: Of the Stair under the Hill
told_in.section: II. Of the Stair under the Hill

events.title: The steward's mistaken tally
events.body: The girl Mòrag Ruadh finds her own small wax-board tally of the hall's candles does not agree with the steward Pàdraig mac Ìomhair's great ledger; he finds the fault his own, a tally-mark set down twice, and sets his sums before her eyes from that evening forward.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Queen Mòrag Ruadh crowned

told_in.book: Of the Thousandth Year
told_in.section: I. Of the Girl Who Kept the Tallies

events.title: Queen Mòrag Ruadh crowned
events.body: Mòrag Ruadh of Clann Raghnaill is crowned at Cathair dhearg. Hers are the first household accounts of a ruler that survive whole.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of Mòrag Ruadh

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The steward's mistaken tally

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Na Seachd Taighean name Mòrag Ruadh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The queen's own book bound

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mòrag Ruadh crowned at nineteen

events.title: Na Seachd Taighean name Mòrag Ruadh
events.body: Na Seachd Taighean, meeting at Taigh na Fèithe on the death of the old king, send word to Cathair dhearg within the month that the crown will go to the girl of Clann Raghnaill who keeps her own small tally beside the steward's; Leabhar a' Chùraim gives four lines and no reason beyond her house and her blood.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Queen Mòrag Ruadh crowned

told_in.book: Of the Thousandth Year
told_in.section: I. Of the Girl Who Kept the Tallies

events.title: The queen's own book bound
events.body: Mòrag Ruadh has a vellum ledger bound within the month of her crowning, clasped in iron rather than silver at her own asking, and enters the cost of her own coronation feast on its first page, signed under her own name.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Queen Mòrag Ruadh crowned

told_in.book: Of the Thousandth Year
told_in.section: I. Of the Girl Who Kept the Tallies

events.title: Mòrag Ruadh crowned at nineteen
events.body: Mòrag Ruadh is crowned at Cathair dhearg at nineteen, the youngest ruler An Talla Dearg has seen since Eilidh Bhàn, and keeps her own small tally beside the steward's from the first day.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Queen Mòrag Ruadh crowned

told_in.book: Of the Thousandth Year
told_in.section: I. Of the Girl Who Kept the Tallies

events.title: The obelisk at Carragh Cnoc bheag cleaned
events.body: The priests of the Hawk at Cnoc bheag clear the moss from the obelisk of Carragh Cnoc bheag and try to read the old letters on it. They cannot, and they write down that they tried.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tòmas clears the moss from Carragh Cnoc bheag

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The queen asks after the unread stone

events.title: Tòmas clears the moss from Carragh Cnoc bheag
events.body: The priest Tòmas mac Aonghais spends a month clearing moss from Carragh Cnoc bheag with wooden scrapers rather than iron, and finds, once the stone stands bare, letters cut deep and old that answer to no shape the schools' own tables keep.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The obelisk at Carragh Cnoc bheag cleaned

told_in.book: Of the Thousandth Year
told_in.section: II. Of the Letters No One Could Read

events.title: The queen asks after the unread stone
events.body: Hearing the report of Carragh Cnoc bheag cleared read to her hall, Mòrag Ruadh enters the cost of Tòmas mac Aonghais's oil and vellum into her own book without comment, and asks only whether the priests mean to try the letters again; the answer she is given is that they do not know.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The obelisk at Carragh Cnoc bheag cleaned

told_in.book: Of the Thousandth Year
told_in.section: II. Of the Letters No One Could Read

events.title: Caol shean's fishing year
events.body: Caol shean, whose boats fish the east coast from the mouth of the Abhainn chaol, lands the greatest catch in its rolls, so great that the salt runs short and half is dried in the wind. The dried fish sells poorly, and the town goes back to salting.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ruairidh mac Neacail hangs the catch in the wind

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Caol shean returns to salting

events.title: The thousandth year
events.body: The vein-house marks the thousandth year of its count with a single measured burning of the coal on Cidhe an Diosail at Seann Skell, and Queen Mòrag Ruadh is there. It is told that the flame burned the colour of the vein, and that the crowd went home without a word.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The queen judges the thousandth year a measure and no more

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The queen's journey to Seann Skell

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The queen's entry for the burning

events.title: Ruairidh mac Neacail hangs the catch in the wind
events.body: When Caol shean's salt runs out on the second day of its greatest catch, the shed-foreman Ruairidh mac Neacail hangs what cannot be salted on lines strung the length of the lower town's lanes rather than let it spoil on the strand.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Caol shean's fishing year

told_in.book: Of the Thousandth Year
told_in.section: III. Of the Nets that Broke the Salt

events.title: The queen judges the thousandth year a measure and no more
events.body: Asked by Na Seachd Taighean whether Taigh na Fèithe's thousandth year deserves a feast or a fast, Mòrag Ruadh judges between them: one burning on the quay the count began from, no more coal in it than an ordinary hearth burns of an evening.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The thousandth year

told_in.book: Of the Thousandth Year
told_in.section: IV. Of the Thousandth Year

events.title: The queen's journey to Seann Skell
events.body: Mòrag Ruadh rides down to Seann Skell over roads already hard with the season's first frosts to stand at Cidhe an Diosail for the thousandth year's burning, a week's journey she makes to see the measure kept rather than take a scribe's report of it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The thousandth year

told_in.book: Of the Thousandth Year
told_in.section: IV. Of the Thousandth Year

events.title: The queen's entry for the burning
events.body: Where another ruler's book might have set down a verse for a thousand years made into one evening's fire, Mòrag Ruadh's own book gives the cost of the coal reckoned to Taigh na Fèithe's weights, and beneath it five words: one handful, nothing more.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The thousandth year

told_in.book: Of the Thousandth Year
told_in.section: VII. Of Baile Ghorm's Blue, and the Queen's Own Entry

events.title: Caol shean returns to salting
events.body: The dried catch sells poorly against salted fish, fetching less at market than a middling salted season the year before; Caol shean lays in salt from that year for a catch half again the size of any it has yet taken.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Caol shean's fishing year

told_in.book: Of the Thousandth Year
told_in.section: III. Of the Nets that Broke the Salt

events.title: Birth of Beathag Fhionn
events.body: Mòrag Ruadh's daughter is born at Cathair dhearg and named Beathag before the child is a day old; the queen's book holds one line for the day and the name, set apart from the ordinary sums in a hand less steady than usual.

told_in.book: Of the Thousandth Year
told_in.section: V. Of the Daughter Born at the Turn of the Year

events.title: The market above the mill-race
events.body: The hill-lords of Baile ghorm hold a market for the farms of the south-east at Cnoc bhàn, above the long mill-race of Muileann fhada. Its common goods are grain, clay and honey. Its rare good is pearls, which the women of the shore take from the mussel beds in the shallows, and which no other market sells.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The mill-race market opened above Muileann fhada

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Sìne nic Ruairidh sells a season's pearls whole

events.title: The mill-race market opened above Muileann fhada
events.body: The hill-lords of Baile ghorm set a single market at Cnoc bhàn above the long mill-race of Muileann fhada to gather the south-east's scattered trade in one place, its rare good the pearls no other market sells in whole parcels.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The market above the mill-race

told_in.book: Of the Thousandth Year
told_in.section: VI. Of the Market above the Mill-Race

events.title: Sìne nic Ruairidh sells a season's pearls whole
events.body: The shore-woman Sìne nic Ruairidh brings a whole season's gathering to the mill-race market's first opening rather than sell it a pearl or two at a time along the road, and a trader of Cathair mhòr pays her more for the lot than she has ever been offered piecemeal.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The market above the mill-race

told_in.book: Of the Thousandth Year
told_in.section: VI. Of the Market above the Mill-Race

events.title: The blue dyers of Baile ghorm
events.body: The dyers of Baile ghorm in the south-east make a fast blue from a marsh plant and a mordant of their own. Cloth of Baile ghorm blue becomes the feast-day dress of the seven houses.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Oighrig nic Ailein fixes Baile ghorm's blue

events.title: Oighrig nic Ailein fixes Baile ghorm's blue
events.body: After ten years changing one thing at a time in her own mordant, the dyer Oighrig nic Ailein finds a mixing that holds Baile ghorm's blue fast through washing after washing; cloth of it is worn within the year at Taigh na Fèithe's midwinter gathering.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The blue dyers of Baile ghorm

told_in.book: Of the Thousandth Year
told_in.section: VII. Of Baile Ghorm's Blue, and the Queen's Own Entry

events.title: Birth of Ailean, son of Beathag Fhionn
events.body: A son, Ailean, is born at Cathair dhearg to Beathag Fhionn, the queen's daughter, then thirty years old, in the one-and-fiftieth year of Mòrag Ruadh's reign.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Death of Queen Beathag Fhionn

told_in.book: Of the Swallowing Cough
told_in.section: I. Of the Cough at Muileann dhomhain

events.title: The swallowing cough at Muileann dhomhain
events.body: A sickness that closes the throat breaks out at Muileann dhomhain and moves along the coast road. The town loses near a third of its people.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Word of the cough reaches An Talla Dearg

events.title: Word of the cough reaches An Talla Dearg
events.body: A rider who has ridden the eighteen miles from Muileann dhomhain without stopping to eat brings word of a sickness that closes the throat. Beathag Fhionn, thirty-nine and eleven years at her mother's right hand, sets down the tally she is reading.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The swallowing cough at Muileann dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Swallowing Cough
told_in.section: I. Of the Cough at Muileann dhomhain

events.title: The cough at Seann Bhral
events.body: The swallowing cough comes to the port of Seann Bhral. The townsfolk themselves close the harbour, and keep the shared meal by leaving food at the town gate.

events.title: Queen Beathag Fhionn closes the roads
events.body: Beathag Fhionn, crowned after her mother Mòrag, closes the coast road between Seann Bhral and Muileann dhomhain and sets reeves at the fords to turn travellers back. The cough goes no further west.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Reeves set at the fords against the cough

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The ford-reeve turns back his own brother

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Death of Queen Mòrag Ruadh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag Fhionn crowned at two-and-forty

events.title: Reeves set at the fords against the cough
events.body: Newly crowned, Beathag Fhionn closes the coast road between Seann Bhral and Muileann dhomhain and sets a reeve at each of the road's six fords with orders to turn back every traveller until the road is released. Chosen mostly from the towns nearest their own crossing, the six hold the road shut for three years, and the cough never crosses west of them.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Queen Beathag Fhionn closes the roads

told_in.book: Of the Swallowing Cough
told_in.section: II. Of the Reeve at the Ford

events.title: The ford-reeve turns back his own brother
events.body: At the crossing nearest Muileann dhomhain, the reeve Seumas mac Coinnich turns back his own brother, who has come to the closed road to reach their dying mother on its far side. He tells him the order holds for every traveller or for none. Their mother dies within the week, and the brothers do not speak again for five years.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Queen Beathag Fhionn closes the roads

told_in.book: Of the Swallowing Cough
told_in.section: II. Of the Reeve at the Ford

events.title: Death of Queen Mòrag Ruadh
events.body: Mòrag Ruadh dies at Cathair dhearg at two-and-eighty, sixty-three years crowned, the longest reign An Talla Dearg has yet entered. Her own ledger, clasped in iron, is closed on its last sum.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Queen Beathag Fhionn closes the roads

told_in.book: Of the Swallowing Cough
told_in.section: I. Of the Cough at Muileann dhomhain

events.title: Beathag Fhionn crowned at two-and-forty
events.body: Beathag Fhionn is crowned in the hall her mother held sixty-three years, forty-two years old and grey already at the temples; the first act set down under her own seal is the closing of the coast road.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Queen Beathag Fhionn closes the roads

told_in.book: Of the Swallowing Cough
told_in.section: II. Of the Reeve at the Ford

events.title: The reeve of Muileann dhomhain walks the lower street
events.body: The old reeve of Muileann dhomhain, who lost a wife and a son to the cough, walks the lower street once a season and writes down which roofs have fallen in since his last walking; the town stands at less than two households in three.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Muileann dhomhain resettled

told_in.book: Of the Swallowing Cough
told_in.section: III. Of the Houses Taken by Lot

events.title: Muileann dhomhain resettled
events.body: Families from the hills about Muileann dhomhain settle the town that the swallowing cough emptied, and take the empty houses by lot. The older families of the town say they never again knew half their neighbours.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The reeve of Muileann dhomhain walks the lower street

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Three brothers from Caol dhearg come down

events.title: Three brothers from Caol dhearg come down
events.body: Three brothers, sons of a hill farmer of Caol dhearg, walk down to Muileann dhomhain and take empty houses on the lower street, land already cleared and walls already standing being cheaper than any new house on a hillside.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Muileann dhomhain resettled

told_in.book: Of the Swallowing Cough
told_in.section: III. Of the Houses Taken by Lot

events.title: A carter's mule lost at Drochaid Ros fhionn
events.body: The road bed of Drochaid Ros fhionn gives way under a salt-carter's mule one wet spring; the mule drowns in its traces and the carter is left standing waist-deep in the Abhainn bheag holding a dripping harness.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Drochaid Ros fhionn repaired

told_in.book: Of the Swallowing Cough
told_in.section: IV. Of the Bridge Built Anew

events.title: Drochaid Ros fhionn repaired
events.body: The arches of Drochaid Ros fhionn, worn by seven centuries of salt carts, are built anew at the cost of the salt-masters of Ros fhionn, whose names are cut on the keystones.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A carter's mule lost at Drochaid Ros fhionn

events.title: Death of Queen Beathag Fhionn
events.body: Queen Beathag Fhionn, who closed the coast road against the cough, dies at Cathair dhearg. Her son Ailean is crowned, first of four kings of that name in the house of Raghnall.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of Ailean, son of Beathag Fhionn

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag Fhionn's last question

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailean crowned at nine-and-fifty

events.title: Beathag Fhionn's last question
events.body: Queen Beathag Fhionn dies at Cathair dhearg at eighty-nine, dictating a grain ruling the morning she takes to her bed; her last question to the young scribe beside her is whether the road between Seann Bhral and Muileann dhomhain still stands open.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Queen Beathag Fhionn

told_in.book: Of the Swallowing Cough
told_in.section: V. Of the Queen's Death

events.title: Ailean crowned at nine-and-fifty
events.body: Ailean, son of Beathag Fhionn, is crowned at Cathair dhearg within the season of his mother's death, nine-and-fifty years old and no longer a young man by any measure the hall can offer.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Queen Beathag Fhionn

told_in.book: Of the Swallowing Cough
told_in.section: V. Of the Queen's Death

events.title: The Baile ghorm blue fades
events.body: The last dyer who knew the Baile ghorm mordant dies without apprentices, having quarrelled with both of hers. The blue that follows is the common blue of the rest of the island.

events.title: The ancestor-posts of Dùn ìseal burned
events.body: Lightning fires the ancestor-posts at Dùn ìseal. The keepers cut the names again from memory and from the custody-book, and own in their roll that some are guesses.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The names cut again at Dùn ìseal

events.title: The names cut again at Dùn ìseal
events.body: Setting new ancestor-posts in the old ground the season after lightning burns the old ones to their footings, the keepers of Dùn ìseal cut the names again as best their own memories and their neighbours' can give them back.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The ancestor-posts of Dùn ìseal burned

told_in.book: Of the Swallowing Cough
told_in.section: VI. Of the Fading Things

events.title: The silting of Ros fhionn
events.body: A shifting bar below Ros fhionn silts up the Abhainn bheag, and the salt barges can no longer reach the quays. The salt-masters take their trade to Caol gharbh on the coast.

events.title: Caol gharbh takes the salt
events.body: Caol gharbh, a fishing village, becomes the salt port of the north-east, and its harbour is dug out and walled with the money of the Ros fhionn masters.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A barge broken at Coinneachadh na h-Amhaich

events.title: The stone on the neck
events.body: Caol gharbh and Caol chrom, the two harbours of the strait, send their headmen to a stone on the neck of land between them, and there settle the dues the salt-boats pay to each. Thereafter they meet at that stone over every quarrel of the strait, and it is called Coinneachadh na h-Amhaich, the meeting of the neck.

events.title: A barge broken at Coinneachadh na h-Amhaich
events.body: A laden barge out of the new harbour at Caol gharbh misjudges the tide at the narrows called Coinneachadh na h-Amhaich and strikes the reef, going down with half her salt still aboard. Both crewmen swim ashore alive. The harbour-masters set the channel's first withy at the rock the following spring.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Caol gharbh takes the salt

told_in.book: Of the Table of Years
told_in.section: I. Of the Narrows and the New Harbour

events.title: The last bridge-keeper of Drochaid Ros fhionn
events.body: The keeper of Drochaid Ros fhionn dies with no daughter or kinsman willing to take up the toll, and the crown's reeve at Ros fhionn lets the office lapse rather than name a stranger to it. The toll-gate stands open thereafter, and no crossing is ever again refused for want of a toll.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Drochaid Ros fhionn falls quiet

told_in.book: Of the Table of Years
told_in.section: I. Of the Narrows and the New Harbour

events.title: The market-court's answer
events.body: Asked whether Ros fhionn's market-court should follow its trade to Caol gharbh, the court's own clerks answer that a court sits where disputes are brought to it, not where the season's cargo happens to lie, and the bench of two-hundred-year oak is not moved.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Drochaid Ros fhionn falls quiet

told_in.book: Of the Table of Years
told_in.section: I. Of the Narrows and the New Harbour

events.title: Seòlaid Ros fhionn withied
events.body: The channel above the flats where the barge was lost is marked from the old bar to open water with a line of withies, Seòlaid Ros fhionn, so that a new pilot may learn the crossing in a season rather than the ten years the old salt-masters once needed.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Drochaid Ros fhionn falls quiet

told_in.book: Of the Table of Years
told_in.section: I. Of the Narrows and the New Harbour

events.title: Drochaid Ros fhionn falls quiet
events.body: The salt going by sea from Caol gharbh, the carts no longer cross Drochaid Ros fhionn. The office of bridge-keeper is done away with, and from this time the bridge is little used.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The last bridge-keeper of Drochaid Ros fhionn

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The market-court's answer

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Seòlaid Ros fhionn withied

events.title: The market-court stays at Ros fhionn
events.body: The salt-masters take their ships to Caol gharbh but leave their market-court on the headland at Ros fhionn, where the weights and tally-sticks are kept. The farms and forges of the north-eastern hills still bring their goods there, and the town keeps its market after it has lost its harbour.

events.title: Seòlaid Ros fhionn
events.body: The salt of Ros fhionn now goes by sea: its boats run down the river past Caol gharbh, round the north-east cape, south along the eastern shore past Seann Tarr and Àth bheag, and west again into the bay below Caol shean, where the salt goes inland. The lane is called Seòlaid Ros fhionn after the town whose salt made it, and the eastern boats keep it long after the salt-pans fail.

events.title: The millers of Muileann shean
events.body: The mills of Muileann shean are fitted with a new gearing, cut in oak, that turns two stones from one wheel. Within a lifetime it spreads to the mills of the north.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The gearing model hung over the millers' door

events.title: Raghnall mac Chaluim sent to Dùn thais
events.body: A priest of the schools of the stag, hearing a shepherd's son of the north-west coast count and recount a flock through an afternoon, tells the boy's father the child belongs at a house of disputation. Raghnall mac Chaluim, fourteen years old, is sent south to Dùn thais the following spring.

told_in.book: Of the Table of Years
told_in.section: II. Of the Millers and the Watcher in the Sea

events.title: The gearing model hung over the millers' door
events.body: The millers of Muileann shean, who first cut the gearing that lets one wheel turn two stones, hang a carved model of it over their own door, a boast that grows quieter with every mill in the north that copies it without asking leave.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The millers of Muileann shean

told_in.book: Of the Table of Years
told_in.section: II. Of the Millers and the Watcher in the Sea

events.title: The Sea-Watcher off the north-west
events.body: Fishers of the thinned north-west coast see the Sea-Watcher, Uilebheist na Mara, near enough to foul their nets. The few boats still working those waters draw further in.

events.title: Birth of Ailean mac Raghnaill
events.body: A son, Ailean, is born in Sliochd Raghnaill, the crown's own house since the reign of Mòrag Ruadh; Leabhar a' Chùraim gives the year and the house and no more.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Death of King Ailean mac Raghnaill

told_in.book: Of the Table of Years
told_in.section: III. Of the Table of Years

events.title: Raghnall begins the count of years
events.body: Raghnall mac Chaluim, thirty years old, begins setting the birth and death rolls of the custodian houses beside those of their tenants at Dùn thais, a labour that will occupy his lamplit evenings for nine years before he brings any finding before Taigh na Deasbaid.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The table of years at Dùn thais

told_in.book: Of the Table of Years
told_in.section: III. Of the Table of Years

events.title: The table of years at Dùn thais
events.body: Raghnall mac Chaluim, a scholar of the druid school at Dùn thais, sets out a table showing that the heads of the custodian houses live some years longer, on the whole, than the tenants of their lands. He asks whether the vein answers the hand that holds it. The finding is set down with unease, and no answer.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Raghnall begins the count of years

links.label: At the same time
links.title: A scholar answered at the reading

events.title: A scholar answered at the reading
events.body: When a scholar of Taigh na Deasbaid calls Raghnall's table a wish dressed in columns, Raghnall offers to run the sums a fifth time on rolls the scholar himself chooses. The scholar sits down without taking up the offer, and the hall remembers the silence longer than the exchange.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The table of years at Dùn thais

told_in.book: Of the Table of Years
told_in.section: III. Of the Table of Years

events.title: The table forbidden
events.body: The king's council forbids the copying of Raghnall mac Chaluim's table of years, and the house of disputation at Dùn thais is shut for a generation. Raghnall's own copy is kept in the vein-house and entered in its inventory.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall's copy entered in Taigh na Fèithe inventory

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: Death of Raghnall mac Chaluim

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: The inventory read past the forbidden line

events.title: Raghnall's copy entered in Taigh na Fèithe inventory
events.body: A custodian who has never met Raghnall mac Chaluim writes to ask whether his working copy of Clàr nam Bliadhnachan still exists and might be sent to the mountain for safekeeping. It is sent, and entered that year in Taigh na Fèithe's own inventory, one line among the galleries and Clachan a' Chrannchuir.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The table forbidden

told_in.book: Of the Table of Years
told_in.section: III. Of the Table of Years

events.title: The great gale at Inis mhòr
events.body: Before the autumn grain fleet has sailed, a gale out of the north-east drives the sea up the river at Inis mhòr higher than any then living had seen. Boats are crushed at their moorings, and the grain fleet does not sail until spring.

events.title: Death of Raghnall mac Chaluim
events.body: Raghnall mac Chaluim dies at Dùn thais in his sixty-sixth year, in the small house the shut school let him keep. The scholars who once argued his table carry him to the school's own burying ground and set a tally-stick at his grave's head, notched once for every year the making of the table cost him.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The table forbidden

told_in.book: Of the Table of Years
told_in.section: IV. Of the Gale, the Boundary and the Pilgrims

events.title: Birth of Iain Ciar
events.body: A son, dark-browed and called Iain Ciar, is born to Ailean mac Raghnaill, then forty years old, the elder of two sons he has by different mothers.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Death of Iain Ciar

told_in.book: Of the Table of Years
told_in.section: V. Of the Two Sons

events.title: Baile ruadh's quarrel with Achadh naomh
events.body: Baile ruadh and Achadh naomh in the far north-east go to law over the grazing on the hills between them. The case is heard three times at Cathair dhearg, and settled by dividing the hills along a stream.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The boundary stones carried home unused

events.title: The boundary stones carried home unused
events.body: After the king's council divides the disputed grazing between Baile ruadh and Achadh naomh along a stream, both shire seats carry home the boundary stones they had brought to argue their claim and set them, unused, into their own walls, where they stand for the rest of the age pointing to a line the water has already made no matter of.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Baile ruadh's quarrel with Achadh naomh

told_in.book: Of the Table of Years
told_in.section: IV. Of the Gale, the Boundary and the Pilgrims

events.title: Pilgrims at Allt an Àigh
events.body: The keepers of the Old Spirits renew the pilgrimage to Allt an Àigh, and a guest-house is built beside the stream for those who come to drink at the right phase of the moon. Its book names pilgrims from every shire.

events.title: The keeping of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr passes to Mairead nic Mhurchaidh
events.body: The last keeper of a long line descended from Iain mac Mhurchaidh, who built the road-house its second byre and began the book of the ox-teams that lodged there, gives over the keeping to his daughter Mairead. She continues the ledger in a hand the ox-drivers of the mining road cannot tell from her father's.

told_in.book: Of the Brothers' Peace
told_in.section: I. Of the Two Courts

events.title: Death of King Ailean mac Raghnaill
events.body: King Ailean mac Raghnaill dies at Cathair dhearg, leaving two sons by different mothers, Iain Ciar and Alasdair Bàn, and each has been told he is the heir.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of Ailean mac Raghnaill

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The blank space on the burial roll

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A refused gift at the feast of Bealltach

events.title: The blank space on the burial roll
events.body: Drawing up King Ailean mac Raghnaill's burial roll, An Talla Dearg's clerks leave a blank space where the heir's name should stand, unable to agree between themselves which of his two sons to write and unwilling to write neither.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of King Ailean mac Raghnaill

told_in.book: Of the Table of Years
told_in.section: V. Of the Two Sons

events.title: The inventory read past the forbidden line
events.body: At the winter reading of Taigh na Fèithe's inventory, the custodian pauses a moment longer than usual over the line entered nearly fifty years before, Clàr nam Bliadhnachan, forbidden to be copied, kept, and then reads on, for the reckoning of that year's coal still has a great deal more of the shelf left to answer for.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The table forbidden

told_in.book: Of the Table of Years
told_in.section: V. Of the Two Sons

events.title: A refused gift at the feast of Bealltach
events.body: A messenger of Alasdair Bàn's, riding to An Talla Dearg with the household's ordinary feast-gift, is turned back at the gate on a pretext of business too full to receive him, the first courtesy either brother's household has refused the other in four years of careful giving.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of King Ailean mac Raghnaill

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The battle of Cnoc naomh

told_in.book: Of the Brothers' Peace
told_in.section: I. Of the Two Courts

events.title: The battle of Cnoc naomh
events.body: Alasdair Bàn's men seize Cnoc naomh and Iain Ciar takes it back. The houses divide four to three, and from this battle Cogadh nam Bràithrean, the Brothers' War, takes its name.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A refused gift at the feast of Bealltach

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The roads set under one following's watch or the other

events.title: The roads set under one following's watch or the other
events.body: With both households calling up every man their houses owe them, the two brothers set every road between the two halves of the island under one following's watch or the other, so that carters who have crossed freely their whole lives must now say plainly which brother's peace they travel under.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The battle of Cnoc naomh

told_in.book: Of the Brothers' Peace
told_in.section: I. Of the Two Courts

events.title: The fire at Ceann mhin
events.body: Alasdair Bàn's ships burn the waterfront of Ceann mhin, which held for his brother. The fire takes the rope stores and the granary, and the town begs its bread of Cathair mhòr.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cathair mhòr feeds Ceann mhin

events.title: Cathair mhòr feeds Ceann mhin
events.body: After Alasdair Bàn's ships burn the rope stores and the granary of Ceann mhin in one night, the town sends to Cathair mhòr, which has taken no side, and Cathair mhòr sends grain enough that no household at Ceann mhin goes hungry that winter.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fire at Ceann mhin

told_in.book: Of the Brothers' Peace
told_in.section: II. Of the Burning of Ceann mhin and the Fall Below Muileann ghlas

events.title: The battle of Muileann ghlas
events.body: Iain Ciar defeats Alasdair Bàn below Muileann ghlas. Alasdair is taken alive; his captains are let go home.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Word of Muileann ghlas reaches the road-house

events.title: Word of Muileann ghlas reaches the road-house
events.body: An ox-driver who turns back from the mountain road rather than push his team through unsettled country brings word of Iain Ciar's victory to An Taigh-seinnse Mòr within the week. Asked where the two brothers now stand to one another, he can only shrug: no one yet knows.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The battle of Muileann ghlas

told_in.book: Of the Brothers' Peace
told_in.section: II. Of the Burning of Ceann mhin and the Fall Below Muileann ghlas

events.title: The brothers' peace at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr
events.body: The brothers make peace at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr, on neutral ground between their lands. Alasdair Bàn gives up his claim and has the lordship of Seann Chwen for life. Iain Ciar is crowned.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The keeper warned a day before

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The benches measured to a finger's breadth

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Ciar crowned at six-and-thirty

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: A reeve of Cathair mhòr presses the keeper for more

events.title: The keeper warned a day before
events.body: A messenger carries word to An Taigh-seinnse Mòr that the two brothers and their followings are riding for the road-house to make their peace there. Mairead nic Mhurchaidh is given a single day's warning and spends the better part of it scrubbing the common-room floor.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The brothers' peace at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr

told_in.book: Of the Brothers' Peace
told_in.section: III. Of the Keeper's Day

events.title: The benches measured to a finger's breadth
events.body: Before the brothers arrive, Mairead nic Mhurchaidh measures the two benches of the common-room board against one another with her own hands until neither runs longer than its match, and sets the same loaf and the same jug of ale at either end, giving neither man the smallest excuse to find a slight in the setting of the table.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The brothers' peace at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr

told_in.book: Of the Brothers' Peace
told_in.section: III. Of the Keeper's Day

events.title: Iain Ciar crowned at six-and-thirty
events.body: With the brothers' peace made at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr, Iain Ciar is crowned at Cathair dhearg, six-and-thirty years old, ten years after his father's burial roll was drawn with a blank where the heir's name should stand.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The brothers' peace at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr

told_in.book: Of the Brothers' Peace
told_in.section: I. Of the Two Courts

events.title: A reeve of Cathair mhòr presses the keeper for more
events.body: Years after the peace, an old reeve of Cathair mhòr asks Mairead nic Mhurchaidh whether the two brothers raised their voices in the long silence at her board. She answers only that she heard nothing through the door she had not already heard from her own oxen, and will say no more of it.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The brothers' peace at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr

told_in.book: Of the Brothers' Peace
told_in.section: III. Of the Keeper's Day

events.title: Alasdair Bàn rides up with a dead captain's news
events.body: Alasdair Bàn goes up to An Talla Dearg himself to carry word of an old captain's death to the king with his own mouth, as the captain asked dying; Iain Ciar receives him without ceremony and sends him home with no larger following than he came with.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Death of Alasdair Bàn

told_in.book: Of the Brothers' Peace
told_in.section: IV. Of the Years the Road Kept Its Peace

events.title: Death of Alasdair Bàn
events.body: Alasdair Bàn dies at Seann Chwen, having kept the peace he made. His lordship returns to the crown.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Alasdair Bàn rides up with a dead captain's news

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Ciar keeps his brother's lordship vacant

events.title: Iain Ciar keeps his brother's lordship vacant
events.body: On Alasdair Bàn's death the lordship of Seann Chwen returns to the crown as the brothers' peace had settled it should. Iain Ciar keeps the lordship vacant for the rest of his own reign rather than grant it to another man, a stubbornness An Talla Dearg's clerks never once ask him to explain.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Alasdair Bàn

told_in.book: Of the Brothers' Peace
told_in.section: IV. Of the Years the Road Kept Its Peace

events.title: White stone from Baile Mòr dhomhain
events.body: Masons of Ceann leathan buy a veined white stone from the hills above Baile Mòr dhomhain for the new front of their temple. From this time the quarry is worked, and its marble goes south by the carriers' road to every town that can pay for it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A mason's slab kept on the road-house mantel

events.title: A mason's slab kept on the road-house mantel
events.body: With the first carts of white marble passing south from the quarries above Baile Mòr dhomhain, Mairead nic Mhurchaidh keeps an unworked slab of the stone, no bigger than a hand, on the mantel above her own hearth, a small vanity she never fully explains to those who ask her why a road-house keeper should want a piece of stone bound for someone else's temple.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: White stone from Baile Mòr dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Brothers' Peace
told_in.section: IV. Of the Years the Road Kept Its Peace

events.title: Pàdraig mac Ruairidh lodges three nights at the road-house
events.body: Gathering material for Leabhar nam Bràithrean, the king's clerk Pàdraig mac Ruairidh stays three nights at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr at his own expense, working each evening by the fire the two brothers once sat beside, and asks the keeper and every passing ox-driver for the tale of the peace. He leaves her a measure of meal for the fire and the bed before he rides on.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The account of the Brothers' War

told_in.book: Of the Brothers' Peace
told_in.section: IV. Of the Years the Road Kept Its Peace

events.title: Iain Ciar's grain law
events.body: Having seen Ceann mhin beg its bread, King Iain Ciar commands that every shire seat keep a year's grain in store against the next war. The law is kept as long as he lives.

events.title: Death of Mairead nic Mhurchaidh
events.body: Mairead nic Mhurchaidh dies at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr in her own bed, at sixty-nine years old, on a night an ox-team lodges in the byre below her window. The keeping of the house passes to a sister's daughter raised under the same roof.

told_in.book: Of the Brothers' Peace
told_in.section: V. Of the Book, and the Meeting at the Far-Off House

events.title: The account of the Brothers' War
events.body: Pàdraig mac Ruairidh, a clerk of King Iain Ciar, writes the story of the Brothers' War. It praises the king at every turn, and it is the only account that survives, to the vexation of later readers.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Pàdraig mac Ruairidh lodges three nights at the road-house

events.title: The inns of the mining roads chartered
events.body: The crown grants a charter to the seven great road-houses of the mining circuit, An Sligeanach Fad' às among them, and makes their keepers answerable for the roads between them. The keepers meet once a year at An Sligeanach Fad' às to settle their accounts.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The keepers' first yearly meeting

events.title: The keepers' first yearly meeting
events.body: The seven keepers of the newly chartered road-houses meet for the first time at An Sligeanach Fad' às to settle their accounts, as the charter now commands once every year. Asked whether the tale of the brothers' peace is as her aunt always told it, the new keeper of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr gives the same answer, word for word.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The inns of the mining roads chartered

told_in.book: Of the Brothers' Peace
told_in.section: V. Of the Book, and the Meeting at the Far-Off House

events.title: Pàdraig mac Ruairidh's death
events.body: The clerk who wrote Leabhar nam Bràithrean in King Iain Ciar's praise dies some years before his king, and no scribe comes after him to keep the tale of the grain law's slow lapsing as he had kept the tale of the war itself.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Death of Iain Ciar

told_in.book: Of the Keel-Song
told_in.section: I. Of the Law That Lapsed

events.title: Death of Iain Ciar
events.body: King Iain Ciar dies at Cathair dhearg. His grain law lapses within a few years, as he had foreseen in a note in his own hand.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Birth of Iain Ciar

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Pàdraig mac Ruairidh's death

events.title: An Taigh-seinnse Òir's beef
events.body: An Taigh-seinnse Òir, at the eastern end of the circuit, is written into the charter-roll as keeping syrupped beef for the custodians' reeves on their rounds. It is the first dish of that house on record; the rest of the entry is a complaint about the price.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The reeve's price complaint at An Taigh-seinnse Òir

events.title: The reeve's price complaint at An Taigh-seinnse Òir
events.body: A custodians' reeve who has eaten the house's secret syrupped beef twice a winter for a decade writes into the charter-roll that the price has risen three years running with nothing else about the dish improved, and asks for a second helping in the same breath.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: An Taigh-seinnse Òir's beef

told_in.book: Of the Keel-Song
told_in.section: II. Of the Houses on the Circuit

events.title: An Taigh-seinnse Reòta
events.body: An Taigh-seinnse Reòta, the road-house on the bare northern road, is snowed in for a whole season with a party of custodians' reeves within. They live on its pickled spinach and fire milk, and their complaint stands in full in the charter-roll.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The keeper's itemised bill

events.title: The keeper's itemised bill
